safi-cedvel:108-108.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّما) kāffa (restrictive) and makfūfa (restricted); (إليّ) is attached to (يوحى); (أنّما) is kāffa and makfūfa..
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أنّما إلهك إله..) is in the position of nominative as nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of the verb يوحى «[Note: meaning: the oneness of your God is revealed to me.. and the meaning is: nothing is revealed to me except the exclusive oneness of the Deity.
It is to be noted that the restrictive ma did not strip (أنّ) of its maṣdar function, so the maṣdar formed from it and the clause after it is the nāʾib fāʿil.]», (الفاء) links the apodosis of an omitted conditional; (هل) is an interrogative particle that carries the sense of a command, i.e. "submit".
The clause «قل ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «يوحى إليّ ... » is in the position of accusative, the content of the saying.
The clause «هل أنتم مسلمون ... » is in the position of jussive, apodosis of an omitted conditional, i.e. "if knowledge of that comes to you, then are you ...".

* Rhetoric:
Restriction (al-qaṣr):
In the words of the Exalted قُلْ إِنَّما يُوحى إِلَيَّ أَنَّما إِلهُكُمْ إِلهٌ واحِدٌ, i.e. nothing is revealed to me except that you have no god but One God, because this is the original purpose of the mission; everything else is among the rulings derived from it. The first innamā restricts the ruling to the thing, as in your saying "innamā yaqūmu Zaydun", i.e. none stands but Zayd; the second restricts the thing to the ruling, as in your saying "innamā Zaydun qāʾimun", i.e. he has no attribute but standing.

safi-cedvel:109-111.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) the first is resumptive; (تولّوا) is a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) with an implied ḍamma on the omitted alif (dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters), in the position of jussive, the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ)..
and (الواو) is the fāʿil (agent); (الفاء) the second links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (على سواء) is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent and the object, i.e. "being equal in their knowledge of it"; (الواو) is a conjunction; (إن) is negative, and (الهمزة) is for interrogation; (قريب) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative «[Note: it may be a fronted khabar (predicate), with the interpreted maṣdar as a postponed mubtadaʾ.
(2, 3) Or a relative noun with the returning pronoun omitted.]»; (أم) is the muttaṣila (connected) type, a conjunction; (ما) is a maṣdar particle «2»; (توعدون) is an imperfect passive verb.. and (الواو) is the nāʾib fāʿil.
The interpreted maṣdar (ما توعدون..) is in the position of nominative, the fāʿil of the assimilated adjective قريب, which takes the place of the khabar.
The clause «إن تولّوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «قل ... » is in the position of jussive, apodosis of the condition, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «آذنتكم ... » is in the position of accusative, the content of the saying.
The clause «إن أدري ... » is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause that is the content of the saying.
The clause «أقريب.. ما توعدون» is in the position of accusative, direct object of the verb أدري, which is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative.
The clause «توعدون ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-maṣdar (ما).
(من القول) is attached to a ḥāl of الجهر, and (ما) is a maṣdar particle «3».
The interpreted maṣdar (ما تكتمون) is in the position of accusative, direct object, its governor being يعلم.
The clause «إنّه يعلم ... » has no grammatical position; it is a resumption within the scope of the saying.
The clause «يعلم ... » is in the position of nominative, khabar of inna.
The clause «يعلم (the second)» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause يعلم (the first).
The clause «تكتمون ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-maṣdar (ما). (الواو) is a conjunction; (إن أدري) is like the first; (لكم) is attached to an adjective of (فتنة); (متاع) is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ «[Note: if the particle of hope (tarajjī) governs متاع, it is conjoined to فتنة.]», its implied form being "هو" or "hādhā"; (إلى حين) is attached to an adjective of (متاع).
The clause «إن أدري ... » is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the preceding clause إن أدري.
The clause «لعلّه فتنة ... » is in the position of accusative, direct object, its governor being أدري, which is suspended by the particle of hope «[Note: The grammarians do not count tarajjī among the suspending elements, but Ibn Hishām and the Kufans count it among them, taking it from Abū ʿAlī in al-Tadhkira.]».

* Rhetoric:
Representative metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-tamthīliyya):
In the words of the Exalted (فَقُلْ آذَنْتُكُمْ عَلى سَواءٍ), where it is likened to one who has a truce with his enemies, then senses their treachery and so throws the covenant back to them, proclaiming and spreading the repudiation, and informs them all of it "عَلى سَواءٍ", i.e. equal in having been notified of it.

safi-cedvel:112-112.t:
* I'rab:
(ربّ) its i'rab has been given earlier «[Note: in verse (89) of this sūra.]»; (بالحقّ) is attached to (احكم), the adjective having been put in place of the described, i.e. "judge with your true judgement"; (الواو) is the conjunction wāw; (الرحمن) is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, nominative; (المستعان) is a second khabar, nominative; (ما) is a maṣdar particle «[Note: or a relative noun with the returning pronoun omitted, the clause after it being its ṣila.]».
The interpreted maṣdar (ما تصفون..) is in the position of genitive through the preposition, attached to (المستعان).
The clause «قال ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «ربّ احكم ... » is in the position of accusative, the content of the saying.
The clause «احكم ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to the vocative.
The clause «ربّنا الرحمن ... » is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause that is the content of the saying.

* Benefits:
- Suspension of operation (al-taʿlīq ʿan al-ʿamal):
It is the nullification of the operation of verbs that govern two objects in form, in the wording but not in the position. Among the suspenders (muʿallaqāt):
1- The lām of commencement (lām al-ibtidāʾ): as in «لقد علموا لمن اشتراه ماله في الآخرة من خلاق».
2- The lām of oath: as in the words of Labīd:
ولقد علمت لتأتينّ منيتي ... إن المنايا لا تطيش سهامها
(I knew well that my death would come to me; indeed the deaths' arrows never miss.)
3- The negative mā: as in «لَقَدْ عَلِمْتَ ما هؤُلاءِ يَنْطِقُونَ».
4- The two negatives lā and in.
5- Interrogation: as in the verse (وَإِنْ أَدْرِي أَقَرِيبٌ) etc., and likewise:
ما كنت أدري قبل عزّة ما البكا ... ولا موجعات القلب حتى تولت
(I did not know, before ʿAzza, what weeping was, nor the heart's aches, until she turned away.)

safi-cedvel:15-15.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive (ما زالت) a defective past verb ... and (ما) is negative (تلك) a demonstrative noun, indeclinable (mabnī) in the position of the nominative, the ism of ما زالت (دعواهم) the khabar (predicate), accusative, its accusative mark being an implied fatḥa on the alif.. (حتّى) a particle of limit and of genitive (حصيدا) a second direct object (mafʿūl bihi), accusative (خامدين) an adjective (naʿt) of (حصيدا) [Note: or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in (جعلناهم).. and it may be a substitute (badal) of (حصيدا).], accusative, its accusative mark being the yāʾ.
Clause: «ما زالت تلك دعواهم ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And clause: «جعلناهم ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-type relative (the implied أن).
And the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أن جعلناهم) is in the position of the genitive after (حتّى), attached to (دعواهم).

* Morphology:
(زالت): it contains an i'lāl (weak-letter change) by substitution; its origin is زولت — the wāw was vowelled after a fatḥa and was changed into an alif; its wazn is فعلت.
(خامدين): plural of خامد, an active participle from the triliteral verb خمد; its wazn is فاعل.

* Rhetoric:
- Comprehensive simile (al-tashbīh al-balīgh):
In His saying, the Exalted, «حَصِيداً خامِدِينَ».
That is: "We made them like the harvested crop and like the extinguished fire"; He likened them to it in their utter uprooting, as you say: "We made them ashes", i.e. like ashes.

safi-cedvel:16-16.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (ما) the first is for negation, and (ما) the second is a relative noun, indeclinable in the position of the accusative, conjoined to (السماء) (بينهما) an adverbial, accusative, attached to an omitted ṣila of ما (لاعبين) an accusative ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of خلقنا; it came in the plural to express magnification.
Clause: «ما خلقنا ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.

* Morphology:
(لاعبين): plural of لاعب, an active participle from the triliteral verb لعب; its wazn is فاعل.

safi-cedvel:17-17.t:
* I'rab:
(لو) a non-jussive conditional particle (لهوا) a first direct object, accusative; the second object is implied, i.e. "that with which one amuses oneself".
And the interpreted maṣdar (أن نتّخذ..) is in the position of the accusative as direct object, its governor being أردنا.
(لدنّا) an adverbial noun, indeclinable on sukūn, in the position of the genitive after من, attached to an omitted second object whose governor is اتّخذناه, i.e. "being" (kāʾinan) (إن) a jussive conditional particle [Note: al-ʿUkbarī allowed it to be a negative particle.], (كنّا) a defective past verb, indeclinable on sukūn, in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and (نا) is the ism of كان.
Clause: «أردنا ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And clause: «نتّخذ ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the particle-type relative (أن).
And clause: «اتّخذناه ... » has no grammatical position; the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional.
And clause: «كنّا فاعلين ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.. and the apodosis of the condition is omitted, i.e. "if We were to do so, We would have taken it".

safi-cedvel:18-18.t:
* I'rab:
(بل) for the transitional iḍrāb (turning from one topic to another) (بالحقّ) attached to (نقذف), (على الباطل) attached to (نقذف), (الفاء) conjunctive in both places (إذا) the "sudden" إذا (الواو) resumptive (لكم) attached to an omitted predicate placed before the mubtadaʾ (الويل), (ما) a maṣdar particle [Note: or a relative noun.. or an indefinite noun that is described, the returning pronoun being omitted in both cases, i.e. "from what you describe Him with".].
And the interpreted maṣdar (ما تصفون) is in the position of the genitive by the preposition, attached to (الويل) — or to the notion of being established (istiqrār) — Clause: «نقذف ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And clause: «يدمغه ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause نقذف.
And clause: «هو زاهق ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause يدمغه.
And clause: «لكم الويل ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And clause: «تصفون ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the particle-type relative (ما) [Note: or the ṣila of the nominal relative.. or it is in the position of the genitive as an adjective of the indefinite (ما)].

* Morphology:
(زاهق): an active participle from the triliteral verb زهق; its wazn is فاعل.

* Rhetoric:
The representational metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-tamthīliyya):
In His saying, the Exalted, «بَلْ نَقْذِفُ بِالْحَقِّ عَلَى الْباطِلِ فَيَدْمَغُهُ», where truth is likened to something solid and falsehood to something soft, and the words "hurling" (qadhf) and "crushing the skull" (damgh) are borrowed for the victory of truth over falsehood, by way of representation; it is as if a solid mass were thrown at the head of the brain of falsehood and split it. In it is an allusion to the loftiness of truth and the lowliness of falsehood, and that the side of the first endures while the second perishes.

safi-cedvel:19-20.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (له) attached to an omitted predicate placed before the mubtadaʾ (من), (في السموات) attached to an omitted ṣila of من (الواو) conjunctive (من) the second is a relative, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the clause لا يستكبرون (عنده) an accusative adverbial attached to an omitted ṣila of من (عن عبادته) attached to (يستكبرون), and (لا) is negative in both places.
Clause: «له من في السموات ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And clause: «من عنده لا يستكبرون ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the resumptive.
And clause: «لا يستكبرون ... » is in the position of the nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من).
And clause: «لا يستحسرون ... » is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the clause لا يستكبرون.
(الليل) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (يسبّحون), (لا) negative.
And clause: «يسبّحون ... » has no grammatical position; explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) [Note: or in the position of the accusative as ḥāl from the agent of (يستكبرون).].
And clause: «لا يفترون ... » is in the position of the accusative as ḥāl from the agent of يسبّحون.

safi-cedvel:21-21.t:
* I'rab:
(أم) it is the detached (munqaṭiʿa) أم with the meaning of بل and the hamza (من الأرض) attached to an omitted second direct object [Note: or attached to an adjective of آلهة, since اتّخذوا is made to include the meaning of "they worshipped".].
Clause: «اتّخذوا ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And clause: «هم ينشرون ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive [Note: that is on the assumption of an interrogative hamza of reproach before it.. and it may be in the position of the accusative as an adjective of آلهة.] And clause: «ينشرون ... » is in the position of the nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم).

* Rhetoric:
Explicit mention of the pronoun:
In His saying, the Exalted, «هُمْ يُنْشِرُونَ».
His saying «هم» must have a purpose, otherwise the sentence stands complete without it. The purpose is, first, that it conveys the sense of exclusivity, as if they were saying: "There is no one here able to bring the dead to life except them"; and second, to record the binding charge against them for ascribing the attributes of divinity to their gods. Allah the Exalted refuted this claim in the verse that follows this one, by the proof of mutual hindrance (dalīl al-tamānuʿ), namely «لَوْ كانَ فِيهِما آلِهَةٌ إِلَّا اللَّهُ لَفَسَدَتا».

safi-cedvel:22-22.t:
* I'rab:
(لو) a non-jussive conditional particle (كان) complete or defective (فيهما) attached to (كان), or to its predicate (آلهة) agent (fāʿil) — or the ism of كان — (إلّا) a noun meaning غير ("other than"), and it together with the Majestic Name is an adjective of آلهة, and the effect of the i'rab appears on the Majestic Name [Note: The intent of the verse is to negate multiple gods and to affirm the One, Unique God. Exception with the accusative is not valid, because the meaning would then be: "Had there been in them gods, Allah not being among them, they would have been corrupted", which would imply that if there were in them gods among whom was Allah, they would not be corrupted — and the invalidity of that is obvious. Likewise the Majestic Name cannot be parsed as a substitute (badal) of آلهة, because the exception is not valid, so the substitution is not valid.].
(اللام) occurring in the apodosis of لو (الفاء) resumptive (سبحان) an absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq) of an omitted verb, accusative (ربّ) an adjective of the Majestic Name, genitive (عمّا) attached to the maṣdar سبحان.. and (ما) is a maṣdar particle [Note: or a relative noun, its returning pronoun omitted.].
Clause: «كان فيهما آلهة ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And clause: «فسدتا ... » has no grammatical position; the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional.
And clause: « (نسبّح) سبحان الله ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And clause: «يصفون ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the particle-type relative (ما).
And the interpreted maṣdar (ما يصفون) is in the position of the genitive by (عن), attached to the maṣdar سبحان.

* Benefits:
Theological or philosophical proofs: His saying, the Exalted, لَوْ كانَ فِيهِما آلِهَةٌ إِلَّا اللَّهُ لَفَسَدَتا. The scholars of theology (ʿulamāʾ al-kalām) said: If gods were multiple, then either they would agree or they would disagree. If they agreed, that would be at the expense of the freedom of one of them or of both; and if they disagreed, their acts would contradict one another. In both cases there is corruption and destruction of the universe. There are also composite philosophical-scientific proofs, which the theologians call the proof from necessity (burhān al-wujūb) and the proof from origination (burhān al-ḥudūth). The theologians used them to demonstrate the existence of Allah. It is most likely that they were drawn from Greek philosophy; and many of the philosophers, ancient and contemporary, Muslim and non-Muslim, were not pleased to reach the reality of God by means of scientific proofs, so they resorted, on the one hand, to the natural disposition (fiṭra), and on the other, to contemplation of the traces of the Deity — order and creativity — whether in the descriptions and forms of nature, or in the human body and soul, or in the kinds of animals and the precision and creativity in their creation. They gave this means of knowing Allah several names, the most important being "the law of creativity and invention". Perhaps the mind and heart find more rest in this field of contemplation, for perceiving the greatness of the Creator, than in those composite scientific laws.
(لو) comes with several meanings:
1- لو: a particle of offering (ʿarḍ), which is requesting with gentleness and kindness, such as: لو تنزل عندنا فتصيب خيرا ("Would that you stayed with us, so that you receive some good").
2- لو: a particle of wishing (tamannī), such as: لو أنّ لنا كرّة فنكون من المؤمنين ("If only we had a return, so that we would be among the believers").
3- لو: a particle of "impossibility of the one because of the impossibility of the other" (imtināʿ li-imtināʿ), a conditional particle for the past; it indicates the non-occurrence of one thing owing to the non-occurrence of another, as in the verse we are dealing with, (لَوْ كانَ فِيهِما آلِهَةٌ إِلَّا اللَّهُ لَفَسَدَتا): the meaning is that corruption did not occur because of the non-existence of any other than Allah; and لو here needs an apodosis, and it is permissible for its apodosis to be joined with the lām.
4- لو is a maṣdar particle, and is called a particle-type relative (mawṣūl ḥarfī) because it is joined to what follows it and puts that into the interpretation of a maṣdar, such as: أودّ لو تجتهد, i.e. "your diligence".

safi-cedvel:23-23.t:
* I'rab:
(لا) negative, and the deputy agent (nāʾib fāʿil) is a latent pronoun, implied as "he", i.e. Allah (عمّا) attached to (يسأل).. and (ما) is a maṣdar particle (الواو) conjunctive.
Clause: «لا يسأل ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive, for confirmation.
And clause: «يفعل ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the particle-type relative (ما).
And clause: «هم يسألون ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the resumptive.
And clause: «يسألون» is in the position of the nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم).

safi-cedvel:24-24.t:
* I'rab:
(أم اتّخذوا.. آلهة) its i'rab has already been given [Note: in verse (21) of this sūra.], (من دونه) attached to an omitted second direct object (هاتوا) an indeclinable imperative verb (jāmid), indeclinable through the dropping of the nūn..
and (الواو) is the agent (من) a relative noun, indeclinable in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (معي) an accusative adverbial attached to an omitted ṣila of من, its accusative mark being the implied fatḥa on the letter before the yāʾ, and (الياء) is the muḍāf ilayhi (من قبلي) like من معي (بل) for the transitional iḍrāb (الفاء) conjunctive, linking the effect with the cause.
Clause: «اتّخذوا ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And clause: «قل ... » has no grammatical position; explanatory resumption.
And clause: «هاتوا ... » is in the position of the accusative as the content of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
And clause: «هذا ذكر ... » has no grammatical position; explanatory resumption — or causal — and clause: «أكثرهم لا يعلمون ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And clause: «لا يعلمون ... » is in the position of the nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أكثرهم).
And clause: «هم معرضون ... » is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the clause لا يعلمون.

* Morphology:
(هاتوا): it is an imperative because it indicates a request and admits the addition of the addressing yāʾ, so one says هاتي; but neither a past nor an imperfect is formed from it, so it is in the status of an indeclinable (jāmid) verb. Some counted it as a verb-noun (ism fiʿl), but a verb-noun does not admit the marks of the verb, and this admits them.

safi-cedvel:25-25.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (من قبلك) attached to (أرسلنا), (رسول) genitive in form, accusative in position, direct object (إلّا) a particle of restriction (إليه) attached to (نوحي), (إلّا) the second is for exception (أنا) a detached pronoun in the position of the nominative, a substitute (badal) for the pronoun of the omitted predicate [Note: or a substitute for the position of لا and its ism, whose position is nominative.], (الفاء) the connecting particle of the apodosis of an implied condition, and (النون) is the nūn of protection (nūn al-wiqāya), and (الياء) which is dropped for lightness is the direct object.
Clause: «ما أرسلنا ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And clause: «نوحي ... » is in the position of the accusative as ḥāl from the agent of أرسلنا or from رسول.
And clause: «لا إله إلّا أنا ... » is in the position of the nominative as khabar of أنّ.
And the interpreted maṣdar (أنّه لا إله ... ) is in the position of the genitive by an omitted preposition, namely the bāʾ, attached to (نوحي), i.e. "We reveal to him that there is no god ...".
And clause: «اعبدون ... » is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if you believe me, then worship me".

safi-cedvel:26-29.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive, and the second object of اتّخذ is implied, i.e. "from the angels" (سبحانه) an absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq) of an omitted verb (بل) for the invalidating iḍrāb (عباد) khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هم" (they), nominative (مكرمون) an adjective of عباد, nominative, its nominative mark being the wāw.
Clause: «قالوا ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And clause: «اتّخذ الرحمن ... » is in the position of the accusative as the content of the saying.
And clause: « (نسبّح) سبحانه ... » has no grammatical position; parenthetical, of supplication.
And clause: « (هم) عباد ... » has no grammatical position; explanatory resumption.
(لا) negative (بالقول) attached to a ḥāl from the agent of يسبقونه (الواو) conjunctive (بأمره) attached to (يعملون).
And clause: «لا يسبقونه ... » is in the position of the nominative as a second khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم) [Note: or it has no grammatical position; explanatory resumption.].
And clause: «هم.. يعملون» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause هم عباد.
And clause: «يعملون» is in the position of the nominative as khabar of the second mubtadaʾ (هم).
(ما) a relative noun, indeclinable in the position of the accusative as direct object (بين) an accusative adverbial attached to an omitted ṣila of ما (ما خلفهم) like ما بين and conjoined to it (إلّا) a particle of restriction (لمن) attached to (يشفعون), (الواو) conjunctive (من خشيته) attached to (مشفقون).
And clause: «يعلم ... » has no grammatical position; giving the reason for what precedes it [Note: or parenthetical.].
And clause: «لا يشفعون ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause هم بأمره يعملون.
And clause: «ارتضى ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative (من).
And clause: «هم.. مشفقون» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause هم بأمره يعملون.
(الواو) conjunctive (من) a conditional noun, mubtadaʾ (منهم) attached to a ḥāl from the agent of يقل (من دونه) attached to an adjective of إله (الفاء) connecting the apodosis (ذلك) a demonstrative noun, mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the clause نجزيه (جهنّم) a second direct object, accusative (كذلك) attached to an omitted absolute object whose governor is نجزي [Note: It is possible that the kāf is a noun meaning مثل ("like"), in the position of the accusative as an absolute object standing in for the maṣdar.].
And clause: «من يقل ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause هم.. مشفقون.
And clause: «يقل ... » is in the position of the nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من).
And clause: «إنّي إله ... » is in the position of the accusative as the content of the saying.
And clause: «ذلك نجزيه ... » is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis of the condition, joined with the fāʾ.
And clause: «نجزيه ... » is in the position of the nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (ذلك).
And clause: «نجزي الظالمين ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.

* Morphology:
(مكرمون): plural of مكرم, a passive participle from the quadriliteral verb (أكرم); its wazn is مفعل with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the ʿayn.
(ارتضى): it contains an i'lāl by substitution; its origin is ارتضي — the yāʾ was vowelled after a fatḥa and was changed into an alif. And the (yāʾ) in the base verb رضي is a substitution for a wāw; its origin is رضو — with ḍamma on the ḍād — because its maṣdar is الرّضوان; then the ḍād was given kasra for ease, then the wāw was changed into yāʾ because it came final after a kasra.

safi-cedvel:30-32.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for the reproachful interrogative (الواو) resumptive [Note: according to the parsers it is for conjunction to something implied.], and the mark of the jussive in (ير) is the dropping of the weak letter..
And the interpreted maṣdar (أنّ السموات..) is in the position of the accusative, filling the place of the two objects of يرى.
(الواو) resumptive (من الماء) attached to an omitted second direct object whose governor is جعلنا [Note: The preposition is attached to (جعلنا), which is made to include the meaning of خلقنا ("We created"), or to a ḥāl.
(2, 4) or attached to (جعلنا), made to include the meaning of خلقنا.. or attached to a ḥāl from فجاج.], (الهمزة) for the rebuking interrogative (الفاء) conjunctive (لا) negative..
Clause: «لم ير الذين ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And clause: «كفروا ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative (الذين).
And clause: «كانتا رتقا ... » is in the position of the nominative as khabar of أنّ.
And clause: «ففتقناهما ... » is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the clause كانتا.
Clause: «جعلنا ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And clause: «يؤمنون ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to an implied resumptive, i.e.:
"Were they ignorant, so that they do not believe?"
(الواو) conjunctive (في الأرض) attached to an omitted second direct object «2», (أن) a maṣdar and accusative particle (بهم) attached to (تميد).
And the interpreted maṣdar (أن تميد..) is in the position of the accusative as object of purpose (mafʿūl li-ajlihi) [Note: or in the position of the genitive by an implied lām together with لا, i.e. لئلّا تميد, the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to (جعلنا).] with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "for fear that it would shake with them".
(فيها) attached to an omitted second direct object «4», (سبلا) a substitute (badal) of (فجاجا) [Note: it is possible that (سبلا) is the first object and (فجاجا) a ḥāl from it — an adjective that has been placed before the described —.].
Clause: «جعلنا ... (the second)» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause جعلنا.. (the first).
And clause: «تميد ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the particle-type relative (أن).
And clause: «جعلنا ... (the third)» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause جعلنا (the first).
And clause: «لعلّهم يهتدون ... » has no grammatical position; explanatory resumption — or causal — and clause: «يهتدون ... » is in the position of the nominative as khabar of لعلّ.
(سقفا) a second direct object, accusative (الواو) resumptive (عن آياتها) attached to (معرضون).
And clause: «جعلنا.. (the fourth)» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the first clause جعلنا.
And clause: «هم.. معرضون» has no grammatical position; resumptive.

* Morphology:
(رتقا): it has the form of the maṣdar of the triliteral verb رتق, and it has the meaning of the passive participle, or is on the assumption of "two things possessing sealing" (dhātay ratq).. its wazn is فعل with fatḥa and sukūn.
(فجاجا): plural of فجّ, a name for the wide road between two mountains; its wazn is فعل with fatḥa and sukūn, and it may carry the sense of a description, as in His saying, the Exalted: لِتَسْلُكُوا مِنْها سُبُلًا فِجاجاً (Sūrat Nūḥ, verse 20); and the wazn of فجاج is فعال with kasra on the fāʾ.
(محفوظا): a passive participle from the triliteral verb حفظ, of the pattern فرح; its wazn is مفعول. It is either in its true sense, i.e. "preserved from every corruption", or it is a rational figurative usage (majāz ʿaqlī) meaning "preserving".

* Benefits:
Kull and baʿḍ ("all" and "some"):
Sībawayh and the majority hold that these two words are definite. He argued for this by the occurrence of the ḥāl after them.
Al-Fārisī denied that, and said: Were they both definite, then "half", "third" and "quarter" would be definite; so these too are on the assumption of an implied muḍāf. The majority rejected al-Fārisī's statement, because the Arabs often omit the muḍāf, whether or not they have it in mind; if they have it in mind, the muḍāf remains definite and the ḥāl is valid after it; otherwise it is not..

safi-cedvel:33-33.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (الذي) a relative, khabar of the mubtadaʾ هو (كلّ) mubtadaʾ, nominative [Note: What made it permissible to begin with an indefinite is its indicating generality, or the assumption of an implied muḍāf.], (في فلك) attached to (يسبحون) Clause: «هو الذي ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And clause: «خلق الليل ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative (الذي).
And clause: «كلّ.. يسبحون» is in the position of the accusative as ḥāl.
And clause: «يسبحون» is in the position of the nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (كلّ) [Note: it may be a second khabar, with the preposition and its genitive noun (في فلك) being the first khabar.].

* Morphology:
(فلك): a name for the orbit of the stars in the sky, and in the speech of the Arabs it is everything round; its wazn is فعل with two fatḥas, its plural is أفلاك on the pattern أفعال.

safi-cedvel:34-35.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (ما) negative (لبشر) attached to an omitted second direct object (من قبلك) attached to an omitted adjective of بشر [Note: or attached to (جعلنا).], (الهمزة) for the reproachful interrogative (الفاء) resumptive (متّ) a past verb, indeclinable on sukūn, in the position of the jussive as the protasis.. and (التاء) is the agent (الفاء) the connecting particle of the apodosis.
Clause: «ما جعلنا ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And clause: «إن متّ ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And clause: «هم الخالدون» is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
(بالشرّ) attached to (نبلوكم), (فتنة) an object of purpose (mafʿūl li-ajlihi), accusative [Note: or a maṣdar in the place of a ḥāl, i.e. "tempting you".. or an absolute object standing in for the maṣdar, so that it meets the meaning of the verb..], (الواو) conjunctive (إلينا) attached to (ترجعون).
And clause: «كلّ نفس ذائقة ... » has no grammatical position; giving the reason for what precedes.
And clause: «نبلوكم ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the causal clause — or resumptive — and clause: «ترجعون ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause نبلوكم.

* Rhetoric:
The implicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-makniyya):
In His saying, the Exalted, «ذائِقَةُ الْمَوْتِ»:
Death is not tasted. So He likened it to food that is not wholesome and not palatable; but its occurrence, and its being something unavoidable, has become like something wholesome and palatable, so there is no escape for any soul from tasting it.

safi-cedvel:36-36.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (إن) a particle of negation (إلّا) a particle of restriction (هزوا) a second direct object, accusative, with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "an object of mockery" (dhā huzuʾin), (الهمزة) for interrogation (هذا) a demonstrative noun, mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the relative (الذي), (الواو) circumstantial (wāw al-ḥāl) (بذكر) attached to (كافرون), and (هم) the second is emphasis (tawkīd) of the first pronoun, in the position of the nominative.
Clause: «رآك الذين ... » is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
And clause: «كفروا ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative (الذين).
And clause: «يتّخذونك ... » has no grammatical position; the apodosis of the non-jussive conditional (إذا) [Note: It is possible that the interrogative clause quoted after the saying (أهذا الذي ... ) is the apodosis of إذا, and in that case the clause يتخذونك is parenthetical.].
And clause: «هذا الذي ... » is in the position of the accusative as the content of the saying, of an implied saying, i.e.:
"They say: Is this the one who ..." and the implied clause of saying is a ḥāl from the agent of يتّخذونك.
And clause: «يذكر ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative (الذي).
And clause: «هم ... كافرون» is in the position of the accusative as ḥāl from the agent of يتّخذونك.

* Rhetoric:
Concision by omission (al-ījāz bi-l-ḥadhf):
In His saying, the Exalted, «أَهذَا الَّذِي يَذْكُرُ آلِهَتَكُمْ»:
The interrogative is for denial and astonishment. It conveys that what is meant is "mentions your gods with evil", and one may be content with the indication of the situation for it, as in His saying, the Exalted, «سَمِعْنا فَتًى يَذْكُرُهُمْ», for mention of an enemy is only ever in evil; and they avoided stating it explicitly out of courtesy to your gods.

* Benefits:
1- «إذا» differs from the conditional particles in whether the apodosis must be linked with the fāʾ or not.
For all the other conditional particles, if "إن" or "ما" occurs in their apodosis, it must be linked with the fāʾ — «unlike إذا», for the apodosis may come stripped of the fāʾ, as in this verse: وَإِذا رَآكَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا إِنْ يَتَّخِذُونَكَ إِلَّا هُزُواً. 2- Can a maṣdar and an indefinite noun come as a ḥāl? The result of what the grammarians said is three views:
a- The school of Sībawayh: that the maṣdar is the ḥāl, and this is the basic rule.
b- The school of al-Mubarrad and al-Akhfash: that it is an absolute object accusative by an omitted governor, and that omitted governor is the ḥāl.
c- The school of the Kufans: that it is an absolute object accusative by the governor before it, and there is no place in it for a ḥāl. Among this is the saying of Abū l-Ṭayyib:
أبلى الهوى أسفا يوم النوى بدني ... وفرق الهجر بين الجفن والوسن (Love, in grief on the day of parting, wore out my body, and separation divided the eyelid from drowsiness)

كفى بجسمي نحولا أنني رجل ... لولا مخاطبتي إياك لم ترني (It suffices for my body in emaciation that I am a man whom, were it not for my addressing you, you would not see)
So أسفا is an absolute object. The implied form: أسفت أسفا ("I grieved a grief").

safi-cedvel:37-37.t:
* I'rab:
(من عجل) a preposition and its genitive noun, ḥāl from الإنسان (السين) a particle of futurity (الفاء) the connecting particle of the apodosis of an implied condition (لا) a prohibitive, jussive-governing particle, and (النون) is for protection.. and (الياء) which is dropped for lightness — or to match the verse endings — is the direct object.
Clause: «خلق الإنسان ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And clause: «سأريكم ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And clause: «لا تستعجلون ... » is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if you ask for anything, do not be hasty".

* Morphology:
(عجل): a samāʿī (heard, non-rule-based) maṣdar of the verb عجل يعجل of the pattern فرح; its wazn is فعل with two fatḥas, and العجل and العجلة are the opposite of slowness.

safi-cedvel:38-38.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (متى) an interrogative noun, indeclinable in the position of the accusative as an adverb of time attached to a predicate placed before the mubtadaʾ هذا (الوعد) a substitute (badal) of ذا — or an explicative apposition (ʿaṭf bayān) —, nominative (كنتم) a defective past verb, indeclinable on sukūn, in the position of the jussive as the protasis.
Clause: «يقولون ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And clause: «متى هذا الوعد ... » is in the position of the accusative as the content of the saying.
And clause: «كنتم صادقين» has no grammatical position; resumptive.. and the apodosis of the condition is omitted, indicated by the preceding speech, i.e. "if you are truthful in your saying, then when is this promise?"

safi-cedvel:39-39.t:
* I'rab:
(لو) a non-jussive conditional particle (حين) an accusative adverb of time attached to the omitted object of يعلم [Note: i.e. "if the disbelievers knew the coming of what was promised, at a time when they will not hold back.." Al-ʿUkbarī made (حين) a direct object whose governor is يعلم, i.e. "if they knew the time of the Fire's not being held back from their faces.."], (لا) negative (عن وجوههم) attached to (يكفّون), (لا) the second is redundant, to confirm the negation (عن ظهورهم) like عن وجوههم, and it is conjoined to it (لا) the third is to confirm the negation (ينصرون) a passive imperfect verb.. and (الواو) is the deputy agent. Clause: «يعلم الذين ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.. and the apodosis of لو is omitted, its implied form being "they would not have hastened the punishment or the arrival of the Hour" [Note: al-Zamakhsharī implied "they would not have been in that state of disbelief and hastening.." and Ibn ʿAṭiyya implied "they would not have" (the source breaks off here).].
And clause: «كفروا ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative (الذين).
And clause: «لا يكفّون» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
And clause: «هم ينصرون» is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause لا يكفّون.
And clause: «ينصرون» is in the position of the nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم).

safi-cedvel:40-40.t:
* I'rab:
(بل) for the transitional iḍrāb, and the agent of (تأتيهم) is a pronoun referring to the Resurrection, which is indicated by their question (بغتة) a maṣdar in the place of a ḥāl [Note: or an absolute object standing in for the maṣdar, as تأتيهم is made to include the meaning of تبغتهم ("takes them by surprise").], accusative (الفاء) conjunctive in both places (لا هم ينظرون) like لا هم ينصرون [Note: in the preceding verse (39).].
Clause: «تأتيهم ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And clause: «تبهتهم ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the resumptive. And clause: «لا يستطيعون ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause تبهتهم.
And clause: «هم ينظرون ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause لا يستطيعون.
And clause: «ينظرون» is in the position of the nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم).

safi-cedvel:41-41.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (اللام) the lām of oath, for an implied oath (قد) a particle of certainty (برسل) a preposition and its genitive noun, the deputy agent of the verb استهزئ (من قبلك) attached to an adjective of رسل [Note: or attached to (استهزئ).], (بالّذين) attached to (حاق), (منهم) attached to a ḥāl from the agent of سخروا (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable in the position of the nominative as agent of حاق (به) attached to (يستهزئون).
Clause: «استهزئ برسل ... » has no grammatical position; the response to an implied oath.
And clause: «حاق ... ما كانوا» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause of the response to the oath.
And clause: «سخروا ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative (الذين).
And clause: «كانوا به يستهزئون» has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative (ما).
And clause: «يستهزئون» is in the position of the accusative as predicate of كانوا..

safi-cedvel:42-42.t:
* I'rab:
(من) an interrogative noun, indeclinable in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the clause يكلؤكم, and the agent of (يكلؤكم) is a latent pronoun referring to من (بالليل) attached to (يكلؤكم) (من الرحمن) attached to (يكلؤكم) with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "from the punishment of the Most Merciful" (بل) a particle of iḍrāb (عن ذكر) attached to (معرضون).
Clause: «قل ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And clause: «من يكلؤكم ... » is in the position of the accusative as the content of the saying.
And clause: «يكلؤكم ... » is in the position of the nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من).
And clause: «هم.. معرضون» has no grammatical position; resumptive.

safi-cedvel:43-43.t:
* I'rab:
(أم) detached (munqaṭiʿa), meaning بل and the hamza (لهم) attached to an omitted predicate placed before the mubtadaʾ آلهة (من دوننا) attached to an omitted second adjective of آلهة (الواو) conjunctive (لا) to confirm the negation (منّا) attached to (يصحبون) with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "from Our punishment" (لا هم يصحبون) like لا هم ينصرون [Note: in verse (39) of this sūra.].
Clause: «لهم آلهة ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And clause: «تمنعهم ... » is in the position of the nominative as an adjective of آلهة.
And clause: «لا يستطيعون ... » is in the position of the accusative as ḥāl from the agent of تمنعهم [Note: or a resumption confirming the denial before it and showing the falsity of their belief.].
And clause: «لا هم منّا يصحبون ... » is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the clause of the ḥāl.
And clause: «يصحبون ... » is in the position of the nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم).

safi-cedvel:44-44.t:
* I'rab:
(بل) for the transitional iḍrāb (هؤلاء) a demonstrative noun, indeclinable in the position of the accusative as direct object (آباءهم) conjoined to the demonstrative noun by the wāw, accusative (حتّى) a particle of limit and of genitive (عليهم) attached to (طال).
And the interpreted maṣdar (أن طال..) is in the position of the genitive by (حتّى), attached to (متّعنا).
(الهمزة) for the reproachful interrogative (الفاء) resumptive — or conjunctive — (من أطرافها) attached to (ننقصها).
And the interpreted maṣdar (أنّا نأتي ... ) is in the position of the accusative as direct object whose governor is يرون.
(الهمزة) for the rebuking, denying interrogative (الفاء) conjunctive.
Clause: «متّعنا ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And clause: «طال.. العمر» has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the implied particle-type relative (أن).
And clause: «لا يرون ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And clause: «نأتي ... » is in the position of the nominative as khabar of أنّ.
And clause: «ننقصها ... » is in the position of the accusative as ḥāl from the agent of نأتي.
And clause: «هم الغالبون» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause يرون [Note: it is possible that it is resumptive.].

* Morphology:
(طال): it contains an i'lāl by substitution; its origin is طول — its imperfect is يطول — the wāw was vowelled after a fatḥa and was changed into an alif.

safi-cedvel:45-45.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّما) the restraining (kāffa) and the restrained (makfūfa) (بالوحي) attached to (أنذركم), (الواو) resumptive (إذا) stripped of the conditional sense, so it is attached to (يسمع), or to the maṣdar الدعاء [Note: or it includes the meaning of the condition, so it is attached to the implied apodosis, i.e. "when they are warned they do not hear".], (ما) redundant (ينذرون) like ينصرون [Note: in verse (39) of this sūra.].
Clause: «قل ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And clause: «أنذركم ... » is in the position of the accusative as the content of the saying.
And clause: «لا يسمع الصمّ ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And clause: «ينذرون» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.

* Rhetoric:
Putting the overt noun in place of the pronoun:
In His saying, the Exalted, «قُلْ إِنَّما أُنْذِرُكُمْ بِالْوَحْيِ وَلا يَسْمَعُ الصُّمُّ الدُّعاءَ إِذا ما يُنْذَرُونَ». The benefit of this device is to put on record against them their feigned deafness, and to qualify the negation of hearing; for the requirement of the context was that He say: "and they do not hear".

safi-cedvel:46-46.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (اللام) the lām that prepares for the oath (إن) a jussive conditional particle (مسّتهم) a past verb, indeclinable on fatḥa, in the position of the jussive as the protasis (من عذاب) attached to an adjective of نفحة (اللام) the lām of oath (يقولنّ) an imperfect verb, nominative, its nominative mark being the retention of the nūn, which has been dropped because of the succession of similar letters, and the omitted (الواو), dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, is the agent, and (النون) is the nūn of emphasis (يا) a particle of alerting (ويلنا) an absolute object of an omitted verb, accusative.. and (نا) is muḍāf ilayhi [Note: see the i'rab of the last part of this verse in verse (14) of this sūra.].
Clause: «مسّتهم نفحة ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And clause: «يقولنّ ... » has no grammatical position; the response to the implied oath.. and the apodosis of the condition is omitted, indicated by the response to the oath.
Clause: «ويلنا» has no grammatical position; parenthetical, of supplication.
And clause: «إنّا كنّا ... » is in the position of the accusative as the content of the saying.
And clause: «كنّا ظالمين» is in the position of the nominative as khabar of إنّ.

* Morphology:
(نفحة): a maṣdar of single occurrence (maṣdar al-marra) from the triliteral verb نفح; its wazn is فعلة with fatḥa and sukūn.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying, the Exalted, «مَسَّتْهُمْ نَفْحَةٌ» there are three intensifications: a- The mention of "touching" (mass), which is less than penetration, and the arrival of something suffices for its occurrence.
b- The sense of scantiness in نفح, for its basis is the blowing of the scent of a thing. It is said: نفحته الدابة, "the animal struck him with the edge of its hoof", and نفحه بعطية, "he gave him a small gift".
c- The construction of the single-occurrence form, which is for the least that the noun applies to.

* Benefits:
نفحة: ism al-marra (noun of single occurrence):
Here it is fitting for us to deal with the mention of the marra (single occurrence) and the hayʾa (manner), and to set out the means of deriving them:
a- Ism al-marra or maṣdar al-marra: both are one. It is formed from the bare triliteral on the pattern فعلة, to show the number of times the action occurred, such as: وقفت وقفة, وقفت وقفتين, and وقفت ثلاث وقفات, etc.
It is formed from what exceeds the triliteral by adding a tāʾ to the maṣdar, such as: أكرمته إكرامة, and سفّرته تسفيرة. And if the maṣdar already contains the tāʾ from the root, then there is mentioned after it something that indicates its number, such as:
رحمته رحمة واحدة or رحمتين.
b- As for ism al-hayʾa or maṣdar al-hayʾa: it is the maṣdar that is mentioned to show the kind of the action or its quality. It is formed from the triliteral on the pattern فعلة, with kasra on its first letter, such as مات ميتة سيئة ("he died an evil death"). And فلان يمشي مشية الأسد ("so-and-so walks the gait of the lion").
And if its verb exceeds the triliteral, its maṣdar is qualified, and it becomes a maṣdar of kind, or ism al-hayʾa, such as أكرمته إكراما جيدا ("I honoured him with a good honouring").
Important remark:
The tāʾ that indicates a single occurrence does not enter verbs of the heart and of the inner self, which are not perceived by the senses, such as ḥusn, jubn and ʿilm; so one does not say: علمته علمة, nor فهمته فهمة, nor صبرته صبرة, etc.

safi-cedvel:47-47.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (القسط) an adjective of الموازين with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "possessing justice" (dhawāt al-qisṭ), accusative (ليوم) attached to (نضع), (الفاء) conjunctive (تظلم) a passive imperfect verb, nominative (نفس) deputy agent, nominative (شيئا) an absolute object standing in for the maṣdar, i.e. "any wrong, great or small" [Note: it may be a direct object, i.e. "anything of good deeds or evil deeds".], (الواو) conjunctive, and the ism of كان is a latent pronoun, implied as "he", referring to the content of what preceded, i.e. the deed (من خردل) attached to an adjective of مثقال [Note: or an adjective of حبّة.] (بها) attached to (أتينا), (الواو) resumptive (بنا) a redundant preposition and a pronoun whose position is the remote (accusative-genitive) one, agent of كفى.. (حاسبين) a ḥāl from the first-person plural pronoun [Note: or a tamyīz (specification) of the sentence كفى بنا.], accusative, its accusative mark being the yāʾ.
Clause: «نضع ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And clause: «لا تظلم نفس ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause نضع.
And clause: «إن كان مثقال ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause نضع.
And clause: «أتينا» has no grammatical position; the apodosis of a jussive conditional, not joined with the fāʾ [Note: because the verb here is indeclinable, in the position of the jussive as the apodosis.].
And clause: «كفى بنا حاسبين» has no grammatical position; resumptive.

* Morphology:
(خردل): a collective noun (ism jamʿ) for a plant with a very small grain; its singular is خردلة; its wazn is فعلل with fatḥa on the fāʾ and on the first lām.

safi-cedvel:48-49.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (اللام) the lām of oath, for an implied oath (قد) a particle of certainty (الفرقان) a second direct object, accusative (الواو) conjunctive in both places (ضياء) conjoined to الفرقان, accusative, and likewise (ذكرا), (للمتّقين) attached to (ذكرا).
Clause: «آتينا ... » has no grammatical position; the response to the implied oath.
(الذين) a relative in the position of the genitive as an adjective of المتّقين [Note: or it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هم" (they).], (بالغيب) attached to a ḥāl from the agent in (يخشون), (الواو) conjunctive (من الساعة) attached to the khabar (مشفقون), which is a khabar, nominative, its nominative mark being the wāw.
And clause: «يخشون ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative (الذين).
And clause: «هم ... مشفقون» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the ṣila clause.

* Rhetoric:
Turning from the verbal sentence to the nominal sentence:
In His saying, the Exalted, «وَهُمْ مِنَ السَّاعَةِ مُشْفِقُونَ» there is a turning away from address by a verbal sentence, as the context required, to address by a nominal sentence, to indicate that their state with respect to the Hereafter is constant apprehension.

safi-cedvel:50-50.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (مبارك) an adjective of the khabar ذكر, nominative like it (الهمزة) for the reproachful interrogative (الفاء) for resumption (له) attached to (منكرون), which is the khabar of أنتم.
Clause: «هذا ذكر ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And clause: «أنزلناه ... » is in the position of the nominative as a second adjective of ذكر [Note: it may be a ḥāl, because the indefinite noun has been described.].
And clause: «أنتم له منكرون» has no grammatical position; resumptive.

safi-cedvel:51-52.t:
* I'rab:
(ولقد.. رشده) the i'rab of its like has already been given [Note: in verse (48) of this sūra.], (قبل) an adverbial noun, indeclinable on ḍamma, in the position of the genitive by the preposition, attached to (آتينا), (الواو) conjunctive (به) attached to (عالمين), and the pronoun refers to Ibrāhīm.
Clause: «آتينا ... » has no grammatical position; the response to the implied oath.
And clause: «كنّا به عالمين» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the response to the oath [Note: it is possible that the clause is circumstantial with an implied (قد) or without an implied one.] and the clause carries the sense of giving a reason.
(إذ) an indeclinable adverb, in the position of the accusative, attached to (آتينا) or to (عالمين) [Note: it may be an adverbial noun in the position of the accusative as direct object of an omitted verb, its implied form being "remember".], (لأبيه) attached to (قال), (ما) an interrogative noun, indeclinable in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ whose khabar is (هذه), (التماثيل) a substitute of the demonstrative noun — or an explicative apposition — nominative (التي) a relative noun in the position of the nominative as an adjective of التماثيل (لها) attached to (عاكفون).
And clause: «قال ... » is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
And clause: «ما هذه ... » is in the position of the accusative as the content of the saying.
And clause: «أنتم لها عاكفون» has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative (التي).

* Morphology:
(التماثيل): plural of تمثال, a name for what is made in resemblance to the creation of Allah; its wazn is تفعال with kasra and sukūn; تماثيل has the wazn تفاعيل.

safi-cedvel:53-53.t:
* I'rab:
(لها) attached to (عابدين), which is a second direct object whose governor is وجدنا, accusative, its accusative mark being the yāʾ.
Clause: «قالوا ... » has no grammatical position; explanatory resumption.
And clause: «وجدنا ... » is in the position of the accusative as the content of the saying.

safi-cedvel:54-54.t:
* I'rab:
(لقد كنتم) like لقد آتينا [Note: in verse (48) of this sūra.], and it is a defective verb (أنتم) a detached pronoun in the position of the nominative, emphasis (tawkīd) of the ism of كان (آباؤكم) conjoined to the attached pronoun, the ism of كان (في ضلال) attached to an omitted predicate of كنتم.
Clause: «قال ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And clause: «كنتم ... في ضلال ... » has no grammatical position; the response to the implied oath..
And the implied oath clause is in the position of the accusative as the content of the saying.

safi-cedvel:55-55.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for interrogation (بالحقّ) attached to (جئتنا) [Note: or attached to an omitted ḥāl from the agent of جئت.], (أم) the connected (muttaṣila) one, a conjunction (من اللاعبين) attached to an omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ أنت.
Clause: «قالوا ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And clause: «أجئتنا ... » is in the position of the accusative as the content of the saying.
And clause: «أنت من اللاعبين ... » is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the clause جئتنا.

* Benefits:
- The conjunctive أم:
It is of two kinds: connected (muttaṣila) and detached (munqaṭiʿa).
a- The connected: that after which what follows is connected to what precedes and shares the ruling with it. It is the one that occurs after the interrogative hamza or the hamza of equalization:
An example of the interrogative hamza: أعليّ في الدار أم خالد؟ ("Is ʿAlī in the house, or Khālid?")
And an example of the hamza of equalization: «سَواءٌ عَلَيْهِمْ أَأَنْذَرْتَهُمْ أَمْ لَمْ تُنْذِرْهُمْ». It was called "connected" because neither what precedes it nor what follows it can do without the other.
b- The detached: it is the one that serves to cut off the first speech and begin what follows; its meaning is iḍrāb, as in His saying, the Exalted: «هَلْ يَسْتَوِي الْأَعْمى وَالْبَصِيرُ أَمْ هَلْ تَسْتَوِي الظُّلُماتُ وَالنُّورُ أَمْ جَعَلُوا لِلَّهِ شُرَكاءَ».
Remark: the detached «أم» may include the meaning of the denying interrogative alongside iḍrāb, as in «أَمْ لَهُ الْبَناتُ وَلَكُمُ الْبَنُونَ»!

safi-cedvel:56-57.t:
* I'rab:
(بل) for the invalidating iḍrāb (الذي) a relative in the position of the nominative as an adjective of ربّ السموات (الواو) conjunctive (على ذلكم) attached to (الشاهدين) [Note: Al-ʿUkbarī said: "It is not permissible for it to be attached to (الشاهدين), because that would require the ṣila to precede the relative ..." So (ال) is a relative noun, and (على ذلكم) is attached to the derived adjective, hence it is part of the ṣila..
But there is another opinion, supported by Quranic evidence, that permits the ṣila to precede the relative when confusion is not feared, as in the noble verse above, and as in His saying, the Exalted: «وكانوا فيه من الزاهدين», where the adverbial (فيه) is attached to الزاهدين.
And see verse (20) of Sūrat Yūsuf in this book.], (من الشاهدين) attached to an omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ أنا.
Clause: «قال ... » has no grammatical position; explanatory resumption [Note: the content of the saying is omitted, the implied being: He said: "What you have said is not correct; rather ..."].
And clause: «ربّكم ربّ السموات ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And clause: «فطرهنّ ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative (الذي).
And clause: «أنا ... من الشاهدين» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause ربّكم رب ...
(الواو) conjunctive (التاء) for oath (الله) the Majestic Name, the thing sworn by, genitive, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "I swear" (اللام) the lām of oath (بعد) an accusative adverb attached to (أكيدنّ), (مدبرين) an accusative ḥāl from the agent of تولّوا.
And the interpreted maṣdar (أن تولّوا..) is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
And clause: « (أقسم) بالله ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause ربّكم رب السموات ...
And clause: «أكيدنّ ... » has no grammatical position; the response to the oath.
And clause: «تولّوا ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the particle-type relative (أن).

* Benefits:
- The particles of oath:
The particles of oath are three: the yāʾ (sic), the wāw and the tāʾ. [Translator's note: the source says "al-yāʾ" here; the usual third particle besides the wāw and tāʾ is the bāʾ.]
If the particle of oath is omitted, the thing sworn by is put in the accusative, so you say: «الله لأفعلن». Likewise with every genitive-governing particle: if you omit it, you put the noun after it in the accusative by omission of the preposition, or by removal of the preposition (nazʿ al-khāfiḍ); the expression differs while the meaning is one. We shall return to the discussion of the particles of oath another time, if Allah wills.

safi-cedvel:58-58.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive (جذاذا) a second direct object, accusative (إلّا) a particle of exception (كبيرا) excepted by إلّا, accusative [Note: it is originally an adjective of an omitted described noun, i.e. "except a big idol".] (لهم) attached to an adjective of (كبيرا), (إليه) attached to (يرجعون).
Clause: «جعلهم ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive [Note: it may be conjoined to an implied resumptive demanded by the course of the story, i.e.: "So Ibrāhīm returned to the house of the idols and found food before them and said: Will you not eat? and they did not answer him, so he made them into fragments."] And clause: «لعلّهم.. يرجعون» has no grammatical position; explanatory resumption.
And clause: «يرجعون» is in the position of the nominative as khabar of لعلّ.

* Morphology:
(جذاذا): it was said that it is a maṣdar in singular form; it was said that it is a name for a broken thing like debris (ḥuṭām); and it was said that it is the plural of جذاذة, like زجاج and زجاجة; its wazn is فعال with ḍamma on the fāʾ.

safi-cedvel:59-59.t:
* I'rab:
(من) an interrogative noun, indeclinable in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ [Note: it may be a relative noun, mubtadaʾ, whose khabar is the clause إنّه لمن الظالمين, and the clause فعل is the ṣila.], (بآلهتنا) attached to (فعل), (اللام) the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) for emphasis (من الظالمين) attached to an omitted khabar of إنّ.
Clause: «قالوا ... » has no grammatical position; explanatory resumption.
And clause: «من فعل ... » is in the position of the accusative as the content of the saying.
And clause: «فعل هذا ... » is in the position of the nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من).
And clause: «إنّه لمن الظالمين» has no grammatical position; a resumption within the scope of the saying.

safi-cedvel:60-60.t:
* I'rab:
(فتى) direct object [Note: with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "the speech of a youth"], accusative, its accusative mark being the implied fatḥa on the alif (له) attached to (يقال), (إبراهيم) there are several ways of parsing it: First, it is the deputy agent, with يقال made to include the meaning of يسمّى ("is called").. or the name is intended, not the named.
Second, it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هو" (he) or "this".. and the clause is the content of the saying, i.e. the deputy agent.
Third, it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, its implied form being: "Ibrāhīm is the one who did that".. and the clause is quoted [Note: they also allowed a fourth way, that it be the vocative (munādā), which is remote.].
Clause: «قالوا ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And clause: «سمعنا ... » is in the position of the accusative as the content of the saying.
And clause: «يذكرهم ... » is in the position of the accusative as an adjective of فتى.
And clause: «يقال ... » is in the position of the accusative as a second adjective of فتى [Note: it may be a ḥāl from فتى because it is a description.. and it may be an explanatory resumption, in which case it has no position.].

safi-cedvel:61-61.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) the connecting particle of the apodosis of an implied condition (به) attached to (ائتوا), (على أعين) attached to a ḥāl from the pronoun in (به), i.e. "visibly" or "openly".
Clause: «قالوا ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And clause: «ائتوا به ... » is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if it is he, then bring him ..." and the clause of the condition and its apodosis is in the position of the accusative as the content of the saying.
And clause: «لعلّهم يشهدون ... » has no grammatical position; explanatory resumption.
And clause: «يشهدون» is in the position of the nominative as khabar of لعلّ.

safi-cedvel:62-62.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for interrogation [Note: it may be a real question, for they did not know that he was the doer, or it may be one of confirmation, since they knew he was the doer..], (بآلهتنا) attached to (فعلت).
Clause: «قالوا ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And clause: «أنت فعلت ... » is in the position of the accusative as the content of the saying.
And clause: «فعلت هذا ... » is in the position of the nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أنت).
And clause: «يا إبراهيم ... » has no grammatical position; parenthetical, between the ongoing dialogue.

* Rhetoric:
Feigned ignorance of the one who knows (tajāhul al-ʿārif):
In His saying, the Exalted, «أَأَنْتَ فَعَلْتَ هذا بِآلِهَتِنا يا إِبْراهِيمُ» is a delightful device among their devices, called tajāhul al-ʿārif. It is the speaker's asking about what he truly knows, feigning ignorance, so that the speech comes out as praise or blame, or to indicate the intensity of distraction in love, or with the aim of astonishment, rebuke or confirmation. It is of two kinds: affirmative and negated. The verse we are dealing with is of the affirmative feigned ignorance that takes the course of confirmation.

safi-cedvel:63-63.t:
* I'rab:
(بل) for the transitional iḍrāb (هذا) a substitute of كبيرهم — or an adjective — (الفاء) the connecting particle of the apodosis of an implied condition (كانوا) a defective past verb, indeclinable on ḍamma, in the position of the jussive as the protasis.. and (الواو) is the ism of كان.
Clause: «قال ... » has no grammatical position; explanatory resumption.. and the content of the saying is omitted, i.e.: "It was not you who did that", or some other reply.
And clause: «فعله كبيرهم ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive, within the scope of the saying.
And clause: «اسألوهم ... » is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if they can speak, then ask them".
And clause: «إن كانوا ينطقون (the mentioned one) has no grammatical position; an explanation of the preceding implied condition — or it is resumptive.. and the apodosis clause is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.
And clause: «ينطقون ... » is in the position of the accusative as predicate of كانوا.

* Rhetoric:
Allusion (al-taʿrīḍ):
In His saying, the Exalted, «قالَ بَلْ فَعَلَهُ كَبِيرُهُمْ هذا فَسْئَلُوهُمْ إِنْ كانُوا يَنْطِقُونَ» this is one of the oblique forms of speech (maʿāriḍ al-kalām). What is said of it is that Ibrāhīm's intention, blessings of Allah be upon him, was not to ascribe the act that proceeded from him to the idol, but only to establish it for himself and affirm it for them, in an allusive manner by which he reaches his aim of pressing the argument upon them and silencing them. This is as if your companion said to you, when you had written a letter in an elegant hand, and you are famous for fine handwriting: "Did you write this?" — and your companion is unlettered, not good at writing, and capable only of a corrupt scribble — and you said to him: "No, you wrote it." Your intention in this reply would be to confirm it for yourself while mocking him, not to deny it of yourself and attribute it to the unlettered one or the scribbler [Translator's note: the source text ends here without a final stop, and the word «نفية» appears to be a slip for «نفيه», "denying it"].

safi-cedvel:64-65.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive (إلى أنفسهم) attached to (رجعوا), (الفاء) conjunctive (أنتم) a detached pronoun borrowed for the position of the accusative, emphasis (tawkīd) of the attached pronoun, the ism of إنّ [Note: it may be a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is (الظالمون), and the nominal sentence is the khabar of إنّ.], (الظالمون) khabar of إنّ, nominative, its nominative mark being the wāw.
Clause: «رجعوا ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And clause: «قالوا ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the resumptive.
And clause: «إنّكم.. الظالمون» is in the position of the accusative as the content of the saying.
(على رؤوسهم) attached to a ḥāl from the wāw in (نكسوا), (اللام) the lām of oath, for an implied oath (قد) a particle of certainty (ما) negative, working like ليس — or not working — (هؤلاء) the ism of ما in the position of the nominative — or a mubtadaʾ — And clause: «نكسوا ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause قالوا.
And clause: «علمت ... » has no grammatical position; the response to the implied oath.. and the clause of the oath and its response is in the position of the accusative as the content of an implied saying, which is in the place of a ḥāl from the deputy agent, i.e. "saying: By Allah, you certainly know ...".
And clause: «ما هؤلاء ينطقون» is in the position of the accusative, filling the place of the two objects of علمت, which is suspended (muʿallaq) from working by (ما).
And clause: «ينطقون ... » is in the position of the accusative — or nominative — as khabar of (ما) or of هؤلاء.

safi-cedvel:66-67.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for the denying interrogative (الفاء) conjunctive (من دون) attached to a ḥāl from ما (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable in the position of the accusative as direct object (شيئا) an absolute object standing in for the maṣdar, accusative, i.e. "any benefit, neither little nor much" (الواو) conjunctive.
Clause: «قال ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And clause: «تعبدون ... » is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to an implied clause which is the content of the saying, i.e.: "Do you know that, and yet worship ..?"
And clause: «لا ينفعكم ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative (ما).
And clause: «لا يضرّكم ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the ṣila clause.
(أفّ) a verb-noun (ism fiʿl) of the imperfect, meaning "I am vexed" (atadajjaru), and the agent is a latent pronoun, implied as "I" [Note: it is a maṣdar in al-Suyūṭī's opinion, meaning "stench and ugliness".], (لكم) attached to (أفّ), (الواو) conjunctive (لما) attached to (أفّ), so it is conjoined to (لكم), (من دون) attached to a ḥāl from the omitted object of تعبدون, i.e. "you worship it, being besides Allah" (الهمزة) for the denying interrogative and (الفاء) conjunctive (لا) negative.
And clause: «أفّ لكم ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive, within the scope of the saying.
And clause: «تعبدون ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative (ما).
And clause: «تعقلون ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to an implied resumptive, i.e. "Were you ignorant, so that you do not reason?"

* Benefits:
- Verb-nouns (asmāʾ al-afʿāl):
a- The verb-noun: it is what stands in for the verb in operation and is not affected by governors. It is of two kinds: ad hoc (murtajal) and transferred (manqūl).
b- The ad hoc verb-noun:
It is what was so from the origin as it reached us and has no other usage, such as «أوّه، وأفّ ووي», meaning "I am in pain", "I am vexed" and "I am amazed".
c- The transferred verb-noun:
It is what was transferred from something else; to put it more clearly, it is what had a prior usage and was then transferred to a later usage that carries the meaning of the verb, such as: دونك ومكانك.
And such as عليك وإليك ورويدا وبله وحذار ونزال: it is transferred from the adverbial, and from the preposition and its genitive noun, and from the maṣdar, and it is analogical (qiyāsī) on the pattern فعال.

safi-cedvel:68-68.t:
* I'rab:
(كنتم) a defective past verb — an abrogating one — indeclinable on sukūn, in the position of the jussive as the protasis.
Clause: «قالوا ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And clause: «حرّقوه ... » is in the position of the accusative as the content of the saying.
And clause: «انصروا ... » is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the clause حرّقوه.
And clause: «كنتم فاعلين» has no grammatical position; resumptive, and the apodosis of the condition is omitted, indicated by the preceding speech, i.e. "if you are helpers of them, then help them".

safi-cedvel:69-69.t:
* I'rab:
(نار) a vocative, a specific indefinite noun, indeclinable on ḍamma, in the position of the accusative (كوني) a defective imperative verb, indeclinable through the dropping of the nūn.. and (الياء) is a pronoun in the position of the nominative, the ism of كن (على إبراهيم) attached to (سلاما) [Note: or attached to an omitted adjective of (سلاما).], and the mark of the genitive is the fatḥa, because of its being a proper name and non-Arabic (ʿalamiyya and ʿujma).
Clause: «قلنا ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And clause: «the vocative and its response ... » is in the position of the accusative as the content of the saying.
And clause: «كوني بردا ... » has no grammatical position; the response to the vocative.

* Morphology:
(بردا): a samāʿī maṣdar of the verb برد يبرد of the pattern نصر; its wazn is فعل with fatḥa and sukūn [Note: and its being a maṣdar, an omitted word is implied, i.e. "be possessed of coolness".].

safi-cedvel:70-73.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (به) attached to a ḥāl from (كيدا), (الفاء) conjunctive (الأخسرين) a second direct object, accusative.
Clause: «أرادوا ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And clause: «جعلناهم ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the resumptive.
(الواو) conjunctive in both places (لوطا) conjoined to the third-person pronoun in (نجّيناه), (إلى الأرض) attached to the verb نجّيناه, which is made to include the meaning of أوصلناه ("We brought him to") (التي) a relative noun, indeclinable in the position of the genitive as an adjective of الأرض (فيها) attached to (باركنا) [Note: or attached to a ḥāl from العالمين.], (للعالمين) attached to (باركنا), and the mark of the genitive is the yāʾ, for it is attached to the sound masculine plural.
And clause: «نجّيناه ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause أرادوا or the clause جعلناهم.
And clause: «باركنا ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative (التي).
(الواو) conjunctive in the three places (له) attached to (وهبنا), (نافلة) an accusative ḥāl from يعقوب (كلا) a direct object placed first, accusative (صالحين) a second direct object, accusative, its accusative mark being the yāʾ.
And clause: «وهبنا ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause أرادوا or جعلناهم.
And clause: «جعلنا ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause أرادوا or جعلناهم.
(الواو) conjunctive in the five places (أئمّة) a second direct object, accusative (بأمرنا) attached to (يهدون), which is made to include the meaning of يدعون ("they call") (إليهم) attached to (أوحينا), (لنا) attached to (عابدين), the khabar of كانوا.
And clause: «جعلناهم ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the first clause جعلناهم.
And clause: «يهدون ... » is in the position of the accusative as an adjective of أئمّة.
And clause: «أوحينا ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause جعلناهم.
And clause: «كانوا لنا عابدين» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause جعلناهم.

* Morphology:
(فعل): a samāʿī maṣdar of the triliteral verb فعل of the pattern فتح; its wazn is فعل after its own form, with kasra and sukūn.

* Benefits:
- The land that We blessed:
It is Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem) and the villages around it. It is part of Palestine. It was also said: a district of the land of al-Shām. For the word فلسطين there are two views: either it is attached to the sound masculine plural, so it is parsed like it, or it is a diptote, so it is put in the genitive with the fatḥa in place of the kasra.

safi-cedvel:74-75.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (لوطا) a direct object of an omitted verb that is explained by the one mentioned after it (حكما) a second direct object, accusative (الواو) conjunctive in both places (من القرية) attached to (نجّيناه), (التي) a relative noun, indeclinable in the position of the genitive as an adjective of القرية (فاسقين) a second khabar of (كانوا), accusative [Note: or it is an adjective of قوم, or a ḥāl from it, accusative.], its accusative mark being the yāʾ.
Clause: « (آتينا) لوطا ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And clause: «آتيناه ... » has no grammatical position; explicative.
And clause: «نجّيناه ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the resumptive.
And clause: «كانت تعمل ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative (التي) And clause: «تعمل الخبائث ... » is in the position of the accusative as predicate of كانت.
And clause: «إنّهم كانوا ... » has no grammatical position; explanatory resumption — or causal — And clause: «كانوا قوم سوء ... » is in the position of the nominative as khabar of إنّ.
(الواو) conjunctive (في رحمتنا) attached to (أدخلناه), (من الصالحين) attached to the khabar of إنّ.
And clause: «أدخلناه ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause (آتينا) لوطا.
And clause: «إنّه من الصالحين» has no grammatical position; causal.

* Rhetoric:
1- Figurative usage (al-majāz): In His saying, the Exalted, «وَنَجَّيْناهُ مِنَ الْقَرْيَةِ الَّتِي كانَتْ تَعْمَلُ الْخَبائِثَ» the town is a figure for its people.
2- Figurative usage in His saying, the Exalted, «وَأَدْخَلْناهُ فِي رَحْمَتِنا»: that is, among the people of Our mercy, i.e. We placed him among them and in their number, so the containment is figurative; or into Our Paradise, so the containment is literal and "mercy" is the figure; and it is possible that "mercy" is a figure for prophethood, with the containment figurative as well.

safi-cedvel:76-77.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (نوحا) a direct object of an omitted verb, its implied form being "remember" [Note: it may be conjoined to (لوطا), i.e. "We gave Lūṭ and Nūḥ judgement"... and the same holds for the names of the prophets Dāwūd and Sulaymān.], and it is with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "remember the account of Nūḥ" (إذ) an adverb of past time attached to the implied muḍāf, "the account of Nūḥ" [Note: it may be a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) if (نوحا) is parsed as conjoined to (لوطا).], (قبل) an adverbial noun, indeclinable on ḍamma, in the position of the genitive, attached to (نادى), (الفاء) conjunctive in both places (له) attached to (استجبنا), (أهله) conjoined to the third-person object pronoun in (نجّيناه), (من الكرب) attached to (نجّيناه).
Clause: « (اذكر) نوحا ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And clause: «نادى ... » is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
And clause: «استجبنا ... » is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause نادى.
And clause: «نجّيناه ... » is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause استجبنا.
(الواو) conjunctive (من القوم) attached to (نصرناه), which is made to include the meaning of منعناه ("We protected him") (الذين) a relative noun, an adjective of القوم (بآياتنا) attached to (كذّبوا), (الفاء) conjunctive (أجمعين) an accusative ḥāl from the third-person pronoun in (أغرقناهم) [Note: or emphasis (tawkīd) of the third-person pronoun, which is in the position of the accusative.].
And clause: «نصرناه ... » is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause نجّيناه.
And clause: «كذّبوا ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative (الذين).
And clause: «إنّهم كانوا ... » has no grammatical position; parenthetical — or explanatory resumption — And clause: «كانوا ... » is in the position of the nominative as khabar of إنّ.
And clause: «أغرقناهم ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the ṣila clause of the relative.

safi-cedvel:78-82.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (داود) a direct object of an omitted verb, its implied form being "remember", and it is with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "remember the account of Dāwūd and Sulaymān" [Note: see footnote no. (2) on page (53)], (الواو) conjunctive (إذ) an adverb of time for the past, attached to the implied muḍāf (the account), (في الحرث) attached to (يحكمان), (إذ) an adverb attached to (يحكمان), (فيه) attached to (نفشت), (الواو) circumstantial (لحكمهم) attached to the khabar (شاهدين) [Note: the lām may be redundant, for reinforcement, so (حكم) is accusative in position, the object of شاهدين.].
Clause: « (اذكر) داود ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And clause: «يحكمان ... » is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
And clause: «نفشت ... غنم» is in the position of the genitive, through the annexation of the second (إذ) to it.
And clause: «كنّا.. شاهدين» is in the position of the accusative as ḥāl [Note: or it has no grammatical position; parenthetical between the conjoined and that to which it is conjoined.].
(الفاء) conjunctive (سليمان) a second direct object, accusative, and it is denied tanwīn because of being a proper name and having an added alif and nūn (كلا.. علما) the i'rab of its like has already been given [Note: in verse (72) of this sūra.], (الواو) conjunctive (مع) an accusative adverb attached to (يسبّحن), and Dāwūd is a diptote because of being a proper name and non-Arabic (يسبّحن) an imperfect verb, indeclinable on sukūn.. and (النون) is the agent (الطير) conjoined to الجبال by the wāw, accusative [Note: the wāw may be the wāw of accompaniment, with الطّير as mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment).], (الواو) for conjunction.
And clause: «فهّمناها ... » is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause يحكمان [Note: the third-person pronoun in (فهّمناها) refers to the judgement (ḥukūma).].
And clause: «آتينا ... » has no grammatical position; parenthetical.
And clause: «سخّرنا ... » is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause فهّمناها.
And clause: «يسبّحن ... » is in the position of the accusative as ḥāl from الجبال.
And clause: «كنّا فاعلين ... » is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause سخّرنا [Note: or in the position of the accusative as ḥāl from the agent of سخّرنا, with an implied (قد).].
