(الواو) conjunctive (لكم) attached to an adjective of لبوس [Note: or attached to (صنعة).. and it may be attached to (علّمناه), in which case the interpreted maṣdar is a substitute (badal) of the kāf in لكم, with the preposition repeated.], (اللام) the lām of cause (تحصنكم) an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām (من بأسكم) attached to (تحصنكم).
And the interpreted maṣdar (أن تحصنكم) is in the position of the genitive by the lām, attached to (علّمناه).
(الفاء) the connecting particle of the apodosis of an implied condition (هل) the particle of interrogation.. and the interrogative is in the sense of a command.
And clause: «علّمناه ... » is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause سخّرنا.
And clause: «تحصنكم ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the implied particle-type relative (أن).
And clause: «أنتم شاكرون ... » the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if We have done that for you, then are you thankful?"

* Morphology:
(صنعة): a maṣdar of the triliteral verb صنع, or its maṣdar of single occurrence; its wazn is فعلة with fatḥa and sukūn.
(لبوس): plural of لبس — with kasra and sukūn — a name for the thing worn; the wazn of لبوس is فعول with fatḥa on the fāʾ.
(الواو) conjunctive (لسليمان) attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "We subjected" (الريح) direct object of the implied verb, accusative (عاصفة) an accusative ḥāl from الريح (بأمره) attached to (تجري) [Note: or attached to a ḥāl from the agent of تجري.], (الى الأرض) attached to (تجري), (التي) a relative noun, indeclinable in the position of the genitive as an adjective of الأرض (فيها) attached to (باركنا), (الواو) conjunctive (بكلّ) attached to the khabar of كنّا, which is (عالمين).
And clause: « (سخّرنا) لسليمان ... » is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause علّمناه.
And clause: «تجري ... » is in the position of the accusative as a second ḥāl from الريح.
And clause: «باركنا ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative (التي).
And clause: «كنّا ... عالمين» is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause (سخّرنا).
(الواو) conjunctive (من الشياطين) attached to an omitted predicate placed first [Note: it may be attached to the implied verb سخّرنا in the preceding verse, in which case the relative after it is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to الريح.], (من) a relative noun, indeclinable in the position of the nominative as a delayed mubtadaʾ (له) attached to (يغوصون), (عملا) a direct object, accusative (دون) an accusative adverb attached to an adjective of (عملا), (الواو) conjunctive (لهم) attached to the khabar حافظين [Note: the pronoun in (لهم) is the object of the active participle حافظين; the lām came for reinforcement.].
And clause: «من الشياطين من يغوصون» is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause (سخّرنا) [Note: as long as the speech is in the context of the account of Dāwūd and Sulaymān, nothing prevents the nominal sentence from being conjoined to the verbal sentence سخّرنا; and it is possible that the clause is resumptive, in the course of the story of Sulaymān.].
And clause: «يغوصون ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative (من).
And clause: «يعملون ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the ṣila clause.
And clause: «كنّا.. حافظين» is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause من الشياطين من يغوصون ...

* Morphology:
(عاصفة): feminine of عاصف, an active participle from the triliteral verb عصف; its wazn is فاعل.. and see verse (22) of Sūrat Yūnus.

* Rhetoric:
The device of "combining the differing and the harmonious" (jamʿ al-mukhtalif wa-l-muʾtalif):
In His saying, the Exalted, «وَداوُدَ وَسُلَيْمانَ إِذْ يَحْكُمانِ فِي الْحَرْثِ إلخ». This device is that the speaker wishes to put two praised persons on an equal footing, so he brings harmonious meanings in praise of them, and then seeks to give one of them preference over the other, by an addition of merit that does not diminish the praise of the other, so for the sake of that preference he brings meanings that differ from the meanings of the equalising.
In the verse, the beginning equated Dāwūd and Sulaymān, peace be upon them, in their fitness for judging, then the end gave preference to Sulaymān, where He says «فَفَهَّمْناها سُلَيْمانَ»; and a turning (iltifāt) occurred, so He brought what takes the place of that addition by which Sulaymān is preferred, so as to point to equality in merit, so that the merit of age and what follows from it of abundant experience and worldly wisdom stands in the place of the addition by which Sulaymān was preferred in judgement.

* Benefits:
1- The story of the judgement of Sulaymān and Dāwūd about the crop:
History relates that two men came in to Dāwūd, peace be upon him, one the owner of a crop and the other the owner of sheep. The owner of the crop said: "The sheep of this man got loose and fell upon my crop and left nothing of it." So Dāwūd gave judgement in his favour for the necks (i.e. the ownership) of the sheep, in return for the crop. They went out and passed Sulaymān and told him of his father's judgement. He said: "Had I been in charge of your affair I would have judged otherwise." Dāwūd learned of Sulaymān's saying, so he summoned him and adjured him to tell him what he would have judged. He said: "I would give the sheep to the owner of the crop, to benefit from their milk and wool, and I would give the crop to the owner of the sheep, to plant it and tend it until it returns as it was; then I would return each to its owner." Dāwūd approved the verdict of Sulaymān and put it into effect..
2- Of the wonders of Sulaymān's judgement:
Muslim related, from the hadith of Abū Hurayra, who said:
"Two women, each with her son, when the wolf came and took away one of them. This one said: 'It was only your son it took away,' and the other said: 'It was only your son it took away.' They took their dispute to Dāwūd, peace be upon him, and he judged the child to be for the elder. They passed Sulaymān and told him, and he said: 'Bring me a knife that I may split him between you.' The younger said: 'No, may Allah have mercy on you,' so he judged him to be hers.." [Translator's note: the source quotation ends here without a closing quotation mark.]

safi-cedvel:83-84.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (أيّوب إذ نادى) like نوحا إذ نادى [Note: in verse (76) of this sūra.], (الواو) circumstantial.
Clause: « (اذكر) أيّوب ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And clause: «نادى ... » is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
And clause: «مسّني الضرّ ... » is in the position of the nominative as khabar of أنّ.
And the interpreted maṣdar (أنّي مسّني الضرّ) is in the position of the genitive by an omitted preposition, namely the bāʾ, i.e. بأنّي مسّني الضرّ, attached to (نادى).
And clause: «أنت أرحم ... » is in the position of the accusative as ḥāl, and the linking pronoun is implied, i.e. "with me" (bī).
(الفاء) conjunctive (له) attached to (استجبنا), (به) attached to an omitted ṣila of the relative ما (من ضرّ) attached to a ḥāl from the pronoun in (به), (الواو) conjunctive in the three places (أهله) a second direct object, accusative (مثلهم) conjoined to أهله, accusative (معهم) an accusative adverb attached to a ḥāl from مثلهم (رحمة) an object of purpose (mafʿūl li-ajlihi), accusative [Note: or an absolute object of an omitted verb, i.e. "We showed him mercy".], (من عندنا) attached to an adjective of (رحمة), (للعابدين) attached to an adjective of (ذكرى) [Note: or attached to the maṣdar ذكرى.].
And clause: «استجبنا ... » is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause نادى.
And clause: «كشفنا ... » is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause استجبنا.
And clause: «آتيناه ... » is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause استجبنا.

* Benefits:
1- The story of Ayyūb:
It is reported in the narrations that Ayyūb was a Roman man, of the descendants of Isḥāq son of Yaʿqūb. Allah made him a prophet and spread the world out for him, and his family multiplied until he had seven sons and seven daughters, and he had kinds of livestock, and five hundred feddans, followed by five hundred slaves, each slave having a wife and child and palm trees. Allah tried him with the loss of his children, the loss of his wealth, and illness in his body, for eighteen years. His wife said to him one day: "If only you would call upon Allah, perhaps He would remove the affliction from you." He said: "I am ashamed before Allah to call upon Him when the duration of my trial has not reached the duration of my ease, which was eighty years." Allah removed the affliction from him and provided him with much, much wealth and children. 2- The scholars of language held that الضَّرّ (with fatḥa on the ḍād) is harm in anything, whereas الضُّرّ with ḍamma on the ḍād is harm to the person, such as emaciation, illness and distress.
3- Dhū l-Nūn: the epithet of Yūnus son of Mattā, i.e. "the companion of the whale". The difference between ṣāḥib and dhū is that ṣāḥib is used from the lower toward the higher, such as: ṣāḥib Rasūl Allāh ﷺ (a companion of the Messenger of Allah). As for dhū, it is the reverse: it is used from the higher toward the lower, such as: dhū l-jalāl, dhū l-nūn, and dhū l-wizāratayn.

safi-cedvel:85-86.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (إسماعيل) a direct object of an omitted verb, its implied form being "remember" (ذا) conjoined to إسماعيل by the wāw, accusative, its accusative mark being the alif (كلّ) mubtadaʾ, nominative [Note: with the intention of annexation, or indicating generality.], (من الصابرين) attached to an omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ.
Clause: « (اذكر) إسماعيل ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And clause: «كلّ من الصابرين ... » is in the position of the accusative as ḥāl from the names of the prophets who are conjoined.
(الواو) conjunctive (في رحمتنا) attached to (أدخلناهم), (من الصالحين) attached to the khabar of إنّ.
And clause: «أدخلناهم» has no grammatical position; conjoined to an implied resumptive, i.e.:
"We gave them the reward of the patient and admitted them ..."
And clause: «إنّهم من الصالحين ... » has no grammatical position; causal.

* Morphology:
(ذو الكفل): the epithet of the son of Ayyūb, whose name was Bishr; he was sent after his father, and he was given this epithet because he undertook (takaffala) to fast all his days and to stand in prayer all his nights, and to judge between people and not become angry.. or because he has a double share of reward and recompense. And al-kifl is a name for a portion and lot.

safi-cedvel:87-88.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (ذا النون إذ ذهب) like نوحا إذ نادى [Note: in verse (76) of this sūra.], and the mark of the accusative in (ذا) is the alif (مغاضبا) an accusative ḥāl from the agent of ذهب [Note: he was angry with his people for what he suffered from them, and his going away without the permission of his Lord.], (الفاء) conjunctive in both places (أن) the lightened form of the heavy one, and its ism is a latent pronoun; the implied form: أنّنا ("that We") (عليه) attached to (نقدر).
And the interpreted maṣdar (أنّنا لن نقدر..) is in the position of the accusative, filling the place of the two objects of ظنّ.
(في الظلمات) attached to a ḥāl from the agent of نادى (أن) the lightened form of the heavy one, and its ism is the omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), its khabar the clause: (لا إله إلّا أنت) [Note: (أن) may be explicative (tafsīriyya), coming after the verb نادى, which has the meaning of saying without its letters..
And the clause: لا إله إلّا أنت — the i'rab of its like has already been given in verse (25) of the sūra.], (سبحانك) an absolute object of an omitted verb, accusative (من الظالمين) attached to the khabar of كنت.
Clause: « (اذكر) ذا النون ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And clause: «ذهب ... » is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
And clause: «ظنّ ... » is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause ذهب.
And clause: «لن نقدر ... » is in the position of the nominative as khabar of the lightened (أن).
And clause: «نادى ... » is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause ظنّ.
And clause: «لا اله إلّا أنت ... » is in the position of the nominative as khabar of the lightened (أن).
And clause: «سبحانك with its implied verb» has no grammatical position; parenthetical, of supplication.
And clause: «إنّي كنت ... » has no grammatical position; in the nature of a reason for what precedes.
And clause: «كنت من الظالمين» is in the position of the nominative as khabar of إنّ.
(الفاء) conjunctive (له) attached to (استجبنا), (من الغمّ) attached to (نجّيناه), (الواو) the second is resumptive (كذلك) attached to an omitted absolute object whose governor is ننجي [Note: i.e. "We save the believers with a saving like the saving that was accomplished for Yūnus".. It is also possible that the kāf is a noun meaning مثل in the position of the accusative as an absolute object standing in for the maṣdar, being its qualifier..].
And clause: «استجبنا ... » is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause نادى. And clause: «نجّيناه ... » is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause استجبنا.
And clause: «ننجي ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.

* Morphology:
(ذا النون): the epithet of Yūnus son of Mattā. And النون is the whale, an inert noun (ism jāmid), its plural أنوان and نينان.
(مغاضبا): an active participle from the quadriliteral verb غاضب; its wazn is مفاعل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.

safi-cedvel:89-90.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (زكريّا إذ نادى) like نوحا إذ نادى [Note: in verse (76) of this sūra.], (ربّ) a vocative muḍāf, accusative, its accusative mark being the implied fatḥa on the letter before the yāʾ, which is dropped for lightness.. and the omitted (الياء) is muḍāf ilayhi (لا) a prohibitive, jussive-governing particle, and (النون) is for protection in (تذرني), (فردا) an accusative ḥāl from the first-person pronoun [Note: or a second direct object if the verb تذر is counted among the verbs of transformation.], (الواو) conjunctive..
Clause: « (اذكر) زكريّا ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And clause: «نادى ... » is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
And clause: «the vocative and its response ... » has no grammatical position; an explanation of the verb of calling [Note: or in the position of the accusative as the content of an implied saying, i.e. "saying"].
And clause: «لا تذرني ... » has no grammatical position; the response to the vocative.
And clause: «أنت خير ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to an implied clause, i.e.: "and grant me an heir, and You are the best ..."
(الفاء) conjunctive (له) attached to (استجبنا), and the second (له) is attached to (وهبنا), and the third (له) is attached to (أصلحنا) (في الخيرات) attached to (يسارعون), (رغبا) a maṣdar in the place of a ḥāl [Note: or an absolute object standing in for the maṣdar that meets its verb in meaning, i.e. "they desire Us with desire and fear Us with fear".. or an object of purpose.], accusative, i.e. "desiring" (لنا) attached to (خاشعين).
And clause: «استجبنا ... » is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause نادى.
And clause: «وهبنا ... » is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause استجبنا.
And clause: «أصلحنا ... » is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause استجبنا.
And clause: «إنّهم كانوا ... » has no grammatical position; causal.
And clause: «كانوا يسارعون ... » is in the position of the nominative as khabar of إنّ.
And clause: «يسارعون ... » is in the position of the accusative as predicate of كانوا.
And clause: «يدعوننا ... » is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the clause يسارعون.
And clause: «كانوا لنا خاشعين» is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the clause كانوا يسارعون.

* Morphology:
(رغبا): a samāʿī maṣdar of the verb رغب يرغب إليه of the pattern فرح, meaning "he supplicated earnestly"; its wazn is فعل with two fatḥas, and there are other maṣdars for the verb: رغبى (with fatḥa or ḍamma on the rāʾ and sukūn on the ghayn), رغبة (with fatḥa or ḍamma on the rāʾ and sukūn on the ghayn), رغبوت (with two fatḥas), رغبان (with two fatḥas), and رغباء (with fatḥa and sukūn).
(رهبا): a samāʿī maṣdar of the verb رهب يرهب of the pattern فرح; its wazn is فعل with two fatḥas, and there are other maṣdars for the verb: رهبة (with fatḥa on the rāʾ and sukūn on the hāʾ), رهب (with ḍamma or fatḥa on the rāʾ and sukūn on the hāʾ), and رهبان (with ḍamma and sukūn, and with two fatḥas).

safi-cedvel:91-91.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (التي) a relative noun, indeclinable in the position of the accusative as direct object of an omitted verb, its implied form being "remember" [Note: it may be a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, the implied form being: "in what is recited to you is she who.."; and it may be conjoined to زكريّا (89).]. (الفاء) conjunctive (فيها) attached to (نفخنا) with two omitted muḍāfs, i.e. "into the opening of her garment" (من روحنا) attached to (نفخنا), (ابنها) conjoined to the pronoun in (جعلناها) by the wāw, accusative (آية) a second direct object, accusative (للعالمين) attached to an omitted adjective of (آية).
Clause: « (اذكر) التي ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And clause: «أحصنت ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative (التي).
And clause: «نفخنا ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the ṣila clause.
And clause: «جعلناها ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the ṣila clause.

* Morphology:
(فرجها): al-faraj of a garment is the slit, and of a person his private part; an inert noun (ism jāmid); its wazn is فعل with fatḥa and sukūn.

safi-cedvel:92-92.t:
* I'rab:
(أمّة) an accusative ḥāl from أمّتكم [Note: the governor of the ḥāl is the sense of emphasis in إنّ, and the ḥāl came from an inert noun because it is a description.], (الواو) conjunctive (الفاء) the connecting particle of the apodosis of an implied condition and (النون) is the nūn of protection and the omitted (الياء) is the direct object.
Clause: «إنّ هذه أمّتكم ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And clause: «أنا ربّكم ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the resumptive.
And clause: «اعبدون» is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if you believe in me, then worship me".

safi-cedvel:93-93.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (أمرهم) a direct object, accusative, the verb being made to include the meaning of قطعوا ("they cut up") [Note: it may be accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "they became divided in their affair".. and in both views it is with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "the affair of their religion".], (بينهم) an accusative adverb attached to (تقطّعوا), (كلّ) mubtadaʾ, nominative [Note: with the intention of annexation.], (إلينا) attached to (راجعون) Clause: «تقطّعوا ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And clause: «كلّ.. راجعون» has no grammatical position; resumptive.

* Rhetoric:
- Turning (iltifāt) in His saying, the Exalted, وَتَقَطَّعُوا أَمْرَهُمْ بَيْنَهُمْ. The original speech was: وتقطعتم أمركم بينكم, in the second person; then it turned to the third person, in order to denounce what they did — the splitting up in religion, making it into scattered pieces — and to report that to others, as if it were said: "Do you not see the enormity of what these people committed in the religion of Allah the Exalted, on which all the prophets, peace be upon them, agreed?" In this is a condemnation of disagreement in the fundamentals.

safi-cedvel:94-94.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) conjunctive (من) a jussive conditional noun, indeclinable in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ, its khabar being the clause of the condition (من الصالحات) attached to (يعمل), and من is partitive (الواو) circumstantial (الفاء) the connecting particle of the apodosis (لا) the lā of generic negation (كفران) the ism of لا, indeclinable on fatḥa, in the position of the accusative (لسعيه) attached to an omitted khabar of لا (الواو) conjunctive (له) attached to (كاتبون) with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "for his deeds"; and the pronoun may return to the striving (saʿy), in which case there is no implied word.
Clause: «من يعمل ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause كلّ إلينا راجعون [Note: in the preceding verse (93).].
And clause: «يعمل من الصالحات» is in the position of the nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من).
And clause: «هو مؤمن ... » is in the position of the accusative as ḥāl from the agent of يعمل.
And clause: «لا كفران لسعيه ... » is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
And clause: «إنّا له كاتبون» is in the position of the jussive, conjoined to the clause لا كفران لسعيه.

* Morphology:
(كفران): a samāʿī maṣdar of the triliteral verb كفر like الكفر; its wazn is فعلان with ḍamma and sukūn.
(كاتبون): plural of كاتب, an active participle from the triliteral verb كتب; its wazn is فاعل and the plural فاعلون.

* Benefits:
- فَلا كُفْرانَ لِسَعْيِهِ:
1- "The Ḥijāzī lā": it is the one that works like ليس, rarely, among the Ḥijāzīs. It does not work at all among the Tamīmīs.
2- It may negate oneness and it may negate the genus.
3- What is required for its working is what is required for the working of «ما». We shall give the details elsewhere, by His help, the Exalted.
4- The most common thing is that its khabar is omitted, as in this verse «فَلا كُفْرانَ لِسَعْيِهِ», the implied form being:
"no denial that exists for his striving" — and like the saying of Saʿd ibn Mālik, grandfather of Ṭarafa ibn al-ʿAbd:
من صدّ عن نيرانها ... فأنا ابن قيس لا براح (Whoever turns away from its fires — then I am Ibn Qays; there is no leaving)
And the khabar may be stated explicitly, like the saying of the poet:
تعزّ فلا شيء على الأرض باقيا ... ولا وزر مما قضى الله واقيا (Console yourself, for nothing on earth endures, and no refuge protects from what Allah has decreed)

safi-cedvel:95-95.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (حرام) a khabar placed first, nominative, for the interpreted maṣdar (على قرية) attached to (حرام) with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "upon the people of a town" (لا) redundant — or negative —..
And the interpreted maṣdar (أنّهم لا يرجعون) is in the position of the nominative as a delayed mubtadaʾ, i.e.: "the return of the people of the town to the world is forbidden" — with لا redundant —.. or "their non-return to the Hereafter is impossible" [Note: al-Akhfash permits beginning with حرام without reliance on a negation or an interrogative, and (أنّ), the interpreted maṣdar, is the agent of the maṣdar (حرام), filling the place of the khabar.].
Clause: «حرام.. أنّهم لا يرجعون» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And clause: «أهلكناها ... » is in the position of the genitive as an adjective of قرية.
And clause: «لا يرجعون ... » is in the position of the nominative as khabar of أنّ.

* Rhetoric:
The metaphor in His saying, the Exalted, «وَحَرامٌ عَلى قَرْيَةٍ», i.e. upon the people of a town: so the speech is on the assumption of an implied muḍāf, or "the town" is a figure for its people. And "forbidden" (ḥarām) is borrowed for what is impossible to occur, on the common ground that neither is hoped to be attained.

safi-cedvel:96-97.t:
* I'rab:
(حتّى) a particle of commencement with no effect (إذا) an adverb of future time that includes the sense of a condition, attached to the content of the apodosis, i.e. "the staring of the eyes of those who disbelieved overtook them" (يأجوج) deputy agent of the verb فتحت with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "the outlets of Yaʾjūj and Maʾjūj were opened" (الواو) the wāw of ḥāl (من كلّ) attached to (ينسلون).
Clause: «فتحت يأجوج ... » is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
And clause: «هم.. ينسلون» is in the position of the accusative as ḥāl.
And clause: «ينسلون ... » is in the position of the nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم).
(الواو) conjunctive (الفاء) the connecting particle of the apodosis (إذا) the "sudden" one, to confirm the linking of the apodosis (هي) the pronoun of the matter, mubtadaʾ, nominative (شاخصة) a khabar placed first, nominative (أبصار) a delayed mubtadaʾ, nominative (يا) for alerting (ويلنا) an absolute object of an omitted verb — one not used in the language — (قد) a particle of certainty (في غفلة) attached to an omitted khabar of كنّا (من هذا) attached to (غفلة), (بل) for the transitional iḍrāb.
And clause: «اقترب الوعد ... » is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause فتحت يأجوج.
And clause: «هي شاخصة أبصار ... » has no grammatical position; the apodosis of the condition (إذا) [Note: the clause may be conjoined to an implied clause which is the apodosis, the implied being "they were resurrected", or "they said: Woe to us".].
And clause: «شاخصة أبصار ... » is in the position of the nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هي).
And clause: «كفروا ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative (الذين).
And clause: «يا ويلنا ... » is in the position of the accusative as the content of an implied saying, i.e.:
"They say: Woe to us ..." and the clause of saying — or the implied saying — is a ḥāl from the agent of كفروا.
And clause: «قد كنّا ... » has no grammatical position; explanatory resumption — or causal — And clause: «كنّا ظالمين ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.

* Morphology:
(حدب): a name for the elevated part of the earth; its wazn is فعل with two fatḥas.
(شاخصة): feminine of شاخص, an active participle of the triliteral verb شخص; its wazn is فاعل and the feminine is فاعلة.

safi-cedvel:98-100.t:
* I'rab:
(ما) a relative noun, indeclinable in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the addressee pronoun, the ism of إنّ (من دون) attached to a ḥāl from the omitted object of تعبدون (حصب) khabar of إنّ, nominative (لها) attached to (واردون) [Note: the pronoun in (لها) is the object of the active participle واردون, so the lām here is for reinforcement.].
Clause: «إنّكم ... حصب» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And clause: «تعبدون ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative (ما).
And clause: «أنتم لها واردون» is in the position of the nominative, a substitute (badal) of حصب جهنّم [Note: it may be a ḥāl from جهنّم, which is permissible because the muḍāf is in the status of a part of the muḍāf ilayhi, for Jahannam comprises the fuel, which is part of it.].
The indication in (هؤلاء) is to the idols (كلّ) mubtadaʾ, nominative [Note: with the intention of annexation, i.e. "every group of the worshippers and the worshipped"] (فيها) attached to (خالدون), the khabar.
And clause: «كان هؤلاء آلهة ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive, within the scope of the preceding address.
And clause: «ما وردوها ... » has no grammatical position; the apodosis of the non-jussive conditional (لو).
And clause: «كلّ فيها خالدون» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause لو كان هؤلاء.
(لهم) attached to a khabar placed first (فيها) attached to the omitted khabar, (زفير) a delayed mubtadaʾ, nominative (الواو) conjunctive (فيها) the second attached to (يسمعون), and the object of يسمعون is omitted, i.e. "they do not hear anything".. [Note: it may be attached to the verb سبقت.]
And clause: «لهم فيها زفير ... » has no grammatical position; explanatory resumption.
And clause: «هم فيها لا يسمعون» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause لهم فيها زفير.
And clause: «لا يسمعون» is in the position of the nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم).

* Morphology:
(حصب): a name for what is thrown into the fire, i.e. as if it is pelted with it; its wazn is فعل with two fatḥas.
(واردون): plural of وارد, an active participle from the triliteral verb ورد.. and see verse (19) of Sūrat Yūsuf.
And clause: «لهم فيها زفير ... » has no grammatical position; explanatory resumption.
And clause: «هم فيها لا يسمعون» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause لهم فيها زفير.
And clause: «لا يسمعون» is in the position of the nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم). [Translator's note: these last three clauses appear a second time in the source, after the Morphology section.]

safi-cedvel:101-104.t:
* I'rab:
(لهم) attached to (سبقت), (منّا) attached to a ḥāl from الحسنى [Note: it may be attached to the verb سبقت.], and (الحسنى) is the agent, nominative, its nominative mark being the implied ḍamma on the alif, and it is an adjective of an omitted described noun, i.e. "the best station" (عنها) attached to the khabar (مبعدون).
Clause: «إنّ الذين ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And clause: «سبقت.. الحسنى» has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative (الذين).
And clause: «أولئك عنها مبعدون» is in the position of the nominative as khabar of إنّ.
(لا) negative (الواو) the wāw of ḥāl (في ما) attached to (خالدون), the khabar of the mubtadaʾ هم.
And clause: «لا يسمعون ... » is in the position of the nominative as a second khabar of the particle إنّ [Note: it may be in the position of the accusative as ḥāl from the pronoun in مبعدون, or in the position of the nominative as a substitute (badal) of (مبعدون).].
And clause: «هم.. خالدون» is in the position of the accusative as ḥāl from the agent of لا يسمعون [Note: it may be resumptive, with no position.].
And clause: «اشتهت أنفسهم» has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative (ما).
(الذي) a relative noun, indeclinable in the position of the nominative as an adjective of يومكم, and the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. "which you were promised" (توعدون) a passive imperfect verb, nominative.. and (الواو) is the deputy agent.
And clause: «لا يحزنهم الفزع ... » is in the position of the nominative as a third khabar of the particle إنّ [Note: or in the position of the accusative as ḥāl from the pronoun of (خالدون), and the clause تتلقّاهم الملائكة is conjoined to it.].
And clause: «تتلقّاهم الملائكة ... » is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the clause لا يحزنهم.
And clause: «هذا يومكم ... » is in the position of the accusative as the content of an implied saying, i.e.:
"They say ..." and the clause of saying is in the position of the accusative as ḥāl from الملائكة.
And clause: كنتم توعدون has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative (الذي).
And clause: «توعدون ... » is in the position of the accusative as predicate of كنتم.
(يوم) a substitute (badal) of the implied returning pronoun in (توعدون) [Note: or attached to the verb لا يحزنهم.. or a direct object of an omitted verb, its implied form being "remember"], accusative (كطيّ) attached to an omitted absolute object whose governor is نطوي (للكتب) attached to the maṣdar طيّ.
And the interpreted maṣdar (ما بدأنا..) is in the position of the genitive by the kāf, attached to an omitted absolute object whose governor is نعيده, i.e. "We shall return it, a return like Our beginning the first creation" [Note: or its governor is نطوي, i.e. "We fold them up a folding like Our beginning the first creation".. and it may be attached to a ḥāl from the pronoun of نعيده, i.e. "We return it in the state of its being similar to the first creation.."], (أوّل) a direct object, accusative, its governor being بدأنا [Note: or a ḥāl from the hāʾ in (نعيده).], (وعدا) an absolute object, accusative, of an omitted verb (علينا) attached to an adjective of (وعدا)..
And clause: «نطوي ... » is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
And clause: «بدأنا ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the particle-type relative (ما).
And clause: «نعيده» has no grammatical position; explanatory resumption.
And clause: « (وعدنا) وعدا ... » has no grammatical position; explanatory resumption.
And clause: «إنّا كنّا فاعلين» has no grammatical position; a resumption confirming the meaning of what preceded.
And clause: «كنّا فاعلين» is in the position of the nominative as khabar of إنّ.

* Morphology:
(مبعدون): plural of مبعد, a passive participle from the quadriliteral verb أبعد; its wazn is مفعل with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the ʿayn.
(حسيس): a samāʿī maṣdar — subject to an approximate rule — of the triliteral verb حسّ; its wazn is فعيل.. and so the maṣdar pattern comes for a verb denoting a sound, and it also comes on the pattern فعال with ḍamma on the fāʾ, like صراخ.
(اشتهت): it contains an i'lāl by deletion, because of the meeting of two quiescent letters: the quiescent alif before the quiescent tāʾ was dropped; its wazn is افتعت.
(الفزع): a samāʿī maṣdar of the verb فزع of the pattern فرح; its wazn is فعل with two fatḥas.
(طيّ): a maṣdar of the triliteral verb طوى; its wazn is فعل with fatḥa and sukūn, and it contains an i'lāl by substitution; its origin is طوي — with a quiescent wāw followed by a yāʾ — and when the wāw and the yāʾ met, the first of them being quiescent, the wāw was changed into yāʾ and assimilated into the other yāʾ.
(السجلّ): a name for the sheet on which one writes; its wazn is فعلل with kasra on the fāʾ, and the kasra of the first lām was moved to the ʿayn to suit the assimilation.

* Rhetoric:
1- Intensification (al-mubālagha):
In His saying, the Exalted, «لا يَسْمَعُونَ حَسِيسَها» is the art of intensification, i.e. the people of Paradise will not hear the faint sound of the Fire when they take up their dwellings in Paradise; the sentence is meant to intensify their deliverance from it.
2- Simile:
In His saying, the Exalted, «كَما بَدَأْنا أَوَّلَ خَلْقٍ نُعِيدُهُ» there is a likening of the repetition to the beginning, in that power embraces both equally. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: what is the 'first creation', that He should repeat it as He began it? I say: its first is its bringing into existence from nothing, so as He brought it into existence first from nothing, He returns it a second time into nothing.
If you ask: why is خلق indefinite? I say: it is like your saying: هو أول رجل جاءني ('he is the first man who came to me'), meaning 'the first of the men', but you made it singular and indefinite, intending to itemise them man by man; so likewise the meaning of (أوّل خلق) is 'the first of creation', in the sense of 'the first of the creatures', because خلق is a maṣdar that is not pluralised."

* Benefits:
- The negative لا:
If it falls on a verb it negates it in the future, and it may negate the past; if it negates the past it must be repeated, such as: «لا أكلت ولا شربت» ("I did not eat nor did I drink"). But if its negation is of the future, repetition is permitted and so is its absence; an instance of repetition is your saying: «زيد لا يقرأ ولا يكتب» ("Zayd neither reads nor writes").
Remark: the negative «لا» may intervene between the preposition and the noun it governs, such as «حضر الطالب بلا كتاب» ("the student came without a book"). There are other remarks about it, which we have passed over for fear of prolixity.

safi-cedvel:105-107.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (اللام) the lām of oath, for an implied oath (قد) for certainty (في الزبور) attached to (كتبنا), and likewise (من بعد).
And the interpreted maṣdar (أنّ الأرض يرثها..) is in the position of the accusative as direct object.
Clause: «كتبنا ... » has no grammatical position; the response to an implied oath.
And clause: «يرثها عبادي ... » is in the position of the nominative as khabar of أنّ.
(في هذا) attached to the khabar of إنّ, and the indication is to the Qur'an (اللام) for emphasis (بلاغا) the ism of إنّ, accusative (لقوم) attached to (بلاغا).
And clause: «إنّ في هذا لبلاغا ... » has no grammatical position; explanatory resumption.
(الواو) conjunctive (ما) negative (إلّا) for restriction (رحمة) an object of purpose (mafʿūl li-ajlihi), accusative [Note: it may be a ḥāl from the kāf, with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "possessing mercy".], (للعالمين) attached to (رحمة) [Note: or attached to an adjective of رحمة.].
And clause: «ما أرسلناك ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the resumptive.

* Morphology:
(الزبور): here it means "the book", and (ال) is generic, i.e. "We wrote in the revealed books"; its wazn is فعول.
(الذكر): here it means the Mother of the Book, which is the Tablet; its wazn is فعل with kasra and sukūn.

safi-cedvel:1-3.t:
* I'rab:
(للناس) attached to (اقترب), (الواو) the circumstantial wāw, (في غفلة) attached to an omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم) [Note: or attached to a ḥāl from the pronoun in (معرضون).], (معرضون) a second khabar, nominative, its sign of nominative being the wāw.
Clause: «اقترب.. حسابهم» has no grammatical position; inceptive (ibtidāʾiyya); and the clause: «هم في غفلة ... » is in the position of an accusative ḥāl from (الناس). (ما) negative, (ذكر) genitive in form, nominative in position, the agent of (يأتيهم), (من ربّهم) attached to (يأتيهم) [Note: or attached to an adjective of (ذكر).. and it was said it is a ḥāl, which he mentions because it was described by the word (محدث); and it was said it is attached to a ḥāl from the pronoun in (محدث), and it was said attached to (محدث).], (محدث) an adjective (naʿt) of (ذكر), genitive, (إلّا) a particle of restriction, (الواو) circumstantial.
And the clause: «ما يأتيهم من ذكر ... » has no grammatical position; in the nature of a cause for what preceded.
And the clause: «استمعوه ... » is in the position of an accusative ḥāl from the object of (يأتيهم), with an implied (قد).
And the clause: «هم يلعبون ... » is in the position of an accusative ḥāl from the agent of «استمعوه».
And the clause: «يلعبون ... » is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم).
(لاهية) an accusative ḥāl from the agent of (يلعبون) [Note: or from the agent of (استمعوه), in which case it is a second ḥāl.], (قلوبهم) the agent of the active participle (لاهية), (الواو) resumptive, (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable in the position of a nominative, a badal (substitute) for the pronoun, the agent of (أسرّوا) [Note: this is one of many aspects in the parsing of this verse.. they also allowed: that the relative be a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the preceding clause (أسرّوا) - and this is Ibn Hishām's choice - or an implied clause whose verb is the operator in the interrogative, i.e.:
"those who did wrong say: is this ..." They also allowed that the relative be the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هم".. or that it be the agent of an omitted verb, its implied form being "says" ... or a badal from the agent of (استمعوه).. or a badal from the object of (يأتيهم).. or a direct object of an omitted verb in the sense of blame.. or that it be the agent of (أسرّوا) and the (الواو) in it a mark of plurality with no grammatical position.. etc.], (هل) an interrogative particle with the sense of negation, (هذا) a mubtadaʾ, (إلّا) a particle of restriction, (بشر) the khabar, nominative, (مثلكم) an adjective of (بشر), nominative [Note: the annexation to the pronoun did not make it definite, because it is deeply rooted in indefiniteness.], (الهمزة) for the interrogative, (الفاء) a conjunction, (الواو) circumstantial.
And the clause: «أسرّوا النجوى ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive [Note: Ibn Hishām chose that the clause be a fronted khabar and (الذين) ظلموا a mubtadaʾ placed later.].
And the clause: «ظلموا ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative (الذين).
And the clause: «هل هذا إلّا بشر ... » is in the position of an accusative, being the content of what was said, of an implied saying [Note: and the implied saying clause is an explanatory resumptive, as if it were said: "What did they say in their secret talk?" The answer: they said "is this ..". And it is possible that the clause be a badal from (النجوى) in the position of an accusative.. or with no grammatical position, as an explanation of (النجوى).].
And the clause: «تأتون ... » is conjoined to an implied resumptive, i.e. "you err, and so you come"..
And the clause: «أنتم تبصرون ... » is in the position of an accusative ḥāl from the agent of (تأتون).
And the clause: «تبصرون ... » is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أنتم).

* Morphology:
(محدث): a passive participle from the quadriliteral أحدث, so it is on the pattern مفعل with a ḍamma on the mīm and a fatḥa on the ʿayn.
(لاهية): the feminine of لاه, an active participle from لها يلهو, and in لاه there is an ʿilāl (weak-letter change) by omission, and in لاهية an ʿilāl by substitution; its origin is لاهوة, the wāw having a vowel after a kasra was changed to a yāʾ.

* Rhetoric:
1- Indefiniteness (al-tankīr):
In His words, the Exalted, «وَهُمْ فِي غَفْلَةٍ»: the indefiniteness in (غفلة) is for magnification and grandeur.

* Benefits:
- His words, the Exalted, وَأَسَرُّوا النَّجْوَى الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا. As for «الذين ظلموا», there are views in its parsing that cover the three states of i'rab; we will not address all the aspects that the scholars of grammar and exegesis took, among which are: badal, mubtadaʾ, agent, khabar, object, and genitive. I say: we will address only the one who claimed that it is an agent: this supposition requires that the verb in His words أَسَرُّوا be pluralised. This supposition belongs to the weak dialects, which the grammarians called "the dialect of 'the fleas ate me'" (lughat akalūnī al-barāghīth), whose proper form would have been to say "the fleas ate me" in the singular verb. Likewise, on the supposition that (الذين) is an agent, the expected text would have been وَأَسَرُّوا النَّجْوَى الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا «the verse».
In our view this supposition is rejected, to avoid weak dialects in the Noble Qur'an, as long as we have, in the parsing of (الذين), aspects that keep us away from places of weakness.

safi-cedvel:4-4.t:
* I'rab:
(في السماء) attached to an omitted ḥāl from (القول), (الواو) a conjunction, (العليم) a second khabar, nominative.
Clause: «قال ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause: «ربّي يعلم ... » is in the position of an accusative, being the content of what was said.
And the clause: «يعلم ... » is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (ربّي).
And the clause: «هو السميع ... » is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause of the content of what was said.

safi-cedvel:5-5.t:
* I'rab:
(بل) for the transitional rejection (iḍrāb intiqālī) in the three places, (أضغاث) the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هو", i.e. what he brought of the Qur'an, (الفاء) the connective of an implied conditional apodosis, (اللام) the lām of command, and the sign of the jussive in (يأتنا) is the dropping of the weak letter, (بآية) attached to (يأتنا), (الكاف) a preposition and particle of comparison [Note: or it is a noun in the sense of "like", in the position of an accusative absolute object standing in for the maṣdar, its governor being (يأتنا).], (ما) a maṣdar particle [Note: it is possible that it is a relative, with the returning pronoun omitted, i.e. "as the former ones were sent with it", and the preposition and its genitive noun an adjective of (آية).], (أرسل) a passive past verb, (الأوّلون) the nāʾib fāʿil, nominative, its sign of nominative being the wāw.
And the interpreted maṣdar (ما أرسل..) is in the position of a genitive by the kāf, attached to an omitted absolute object whose governor is (يأتنا), i.e. "let him bring us a sign, a bringing like the sending of the former ones".
Clause: «قالوا ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause: « (هو) أضغاث ... » is in the position of an accusative, being the content of what was said.
And the clause: «افتراه ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause: «هو شاعر ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause: «يأتنا ... » is in the position of a jussive, the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if it is not as we have said and he was a messenger, then let him bring us a sign".

* Benefits:
His words, the Exalted, بَلْ قالُوا: أَضْغاثُ أَحْلامٍ بَلِ افْتَراهُ بَلْ هُوَ شاعِرٌ: they turned away from their opinion three times, using the particle of rejection «بل». This indicates the extent of their hesitancy, their wavering, their lack of firmness on any opinion, and their bewilderment as to by which door they should approach the Prophet, to weaken his position, discourage his resolve, and make a fool of his opinion. Evil indeed is what they do.
Like one who butts a rock one day to weaken it; it did not harm it, and the mountain goat weakened his own horn.
6- 9
[Translator's note: the trailing "6- 9" is a stray verse-number label in the source text, reproduced as written. The same applies to the trailing labels in the entries that follow.]

safi-cedvel:6-9.t:
* I'rab:
(ما) negative, (قبلهم) an adverb, accusative, attached to (آمنت), (قرية) genitive in form, nominative in position, the agent of (آمنت), (الهمزة) for the interrogative of rebuke, (الفاء) a conjunction.
And the clause: «أهلكناها..» is an adjective of (قرية), in the position of a genitive - by form - and the clause: «هم يؤمنون ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause «آمنت», because the two clauses agree in the sense of negation, since the interrogative is one of rebuke.
And the clause: «يؤمنون ... » is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم).
(ما أرسلنا قبلك) like (ما آمنت قبلهم), (إلّا) a particle of restriction, (رجالا) a direct object, accusative, (إليهم) attached to (نوحي), (الفاء) the connective of an implied conditional apodosis, (كنتم) an incomplete past verb - a nasikh (abrogator) - indeclinable on the sukūn in the position of a jussive, the protasis.. and (تم) is the pronoun, the ism of kāna, (لا) negative.
And the clause: «ما أرسلنا ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause «ما آمنت».
And the clause: «نوحي إليهم ... » is in the position of an accusative, an adjective of (رجالا); and the clause: «اسألوا ... » is in the position of a jussive, the apodosis of an implied condition that what follows explains, i.e.: "if you do not know, then ask.."
And the clause: «كنتم لا تعلمون ... » has no grammatical position; explanatory resumptive.. and the apodosis of the condition is omitted, indicated by the first apodosis.
(الواو) a conjunction, (ما جعلنا) like (ما أرسلنا).. and (هم) is a pronoun, a direct object, (جسدا) a second direct object, accusative [Note: or an accusative ḥāl from the object pronoun in (جعلناهم), in the sense of "We created them" or "We brought them into being", and (جسدا) is either a singular intended as plural or with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "possessors of a body".], and the clause: «ما جعلناهم ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause «ما أرسلنا».
And the clause: «لا يأكلون الطعام» is in the position of an accusative, an adjective of (جسدا).
Clause: «ما آمنت.. من قرية» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause: «ما كانوا خالدين ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause «ما جعلناهم».
(ثمّ) a conjunction, (الوعد) a second direct object, its governor being (صدقناهم), (الفاء) a conjunction, (الواو) a conjunction, (من) a relative noun, indeclinable in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the third-person pronoun in (أنجيناهم).
And the clause: «صدقناهم ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause «جعلناهم».
And the clause: «أنجيناهم ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause «صدقناهم».
And the clause: «نشاء ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative (من).
And the clause: «أهلكنا ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause «أنجيناهم».
10- 13

safi-cedvel:10-13.t:
* I'rab:
(اللام) the lām of an oath, for an implied oath, (فيه) attached to an omitted fronted khabar, (ذكركم) a mubtadaʾ placed later, nominative, (الهمزة) for the interrogative of reproach, (الفاء) a conjunction.
Clause: «أنزلنا ... » has no grammatical position; the response to an implied oath.. and the implied oath clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.
And the clause: «فيه ذكركم ... » is in the position of an accusative, an adjective of (كتابا).
And the clause: «تعقلون ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to an implied resumptive, i.e.:
"Has that been absent from you, so that you do not reason?.."
(الواو) a conjunction, (كم) declarative, a metonym for a number, in the position of an accusative fronted direct object, (من قرية) a tamyīz, (بعدها) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (أنشأنا), and the sign of accusative in (آخرين) is the yāʾ.
And the clause: «قصمنا ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the resumptive - or to the clause of the oath's response - and the clause: «كانت ظالمة ... » is in the position of a genitive, an adjective of (قرية).
And the clause: «أنشأنا ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause «قصمنا».
(الفاء) a conjunction, (لمّا) an adverb with the meaning "when", containing the sense of a condition, attached to the content of the apodosis, i.e. "they were taken by surprise by running from it", and the pronoun in (أحسّوا) refers back to the people of the town, (إذا) the sudden (fujāʾiyya) one, with no grammatical position, (منها) attached to (يركضون) [Note: or attached to a ḥāl from the agent of (يركضون).].
And the clause: «أحسّوا ... » is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «هم منها يركضون ... » has no grammatical position; the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
And the clause: «يركضون ... » is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم).
(لا) a prohibitive that jusses, and the sign of the jussive in (تركضوا) is the dropping of the nūn, (إلى ما) attached to (ارجعوا), and (ما) is a relative, (فيه) attached to (أترفتم), (مساكنكم) conjoined to the relative noun by the wāw, genitive.
And the clause: «لا تركضوا ... » is in the position of an accusative, being the content of what was said, of an implied saying.
And the clause: «ارجعوا ... » is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause «لا تركضوا».
And the clause: «أترفتم ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative (ما).
And the clause: «لعلّكم تسألون ... » has no grammatical position; explanatory resumptive.
And the clause: «تسألون ... » is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of laʿalla.

* Rhetoric:
- Mockery (al-tahakkum):
In His words, the Exalted, وَارْجِعُوا إِلى ما أُتْرِفْتُمْ فِيهِ وَمَساكِنِكُمْ.
This mockery is either because they were generous, spending their wealth to be seen by people and to seek praise, or they were stingy, so that was said to them as mockery upon mockery and rebuke upon rebuke. The meaning is: return to your luxury and your dwellings, perhaps you will be asked tomorrow about what happened to you and what befell your wealth and your dwellings, so that you may answer the questioner from knowledge and observation.

* Benefits:
- لمّا (lammā) and its three aspects:
We pointed out earlier «lammā the adverbial, or temporal». Here we will present to the reader «lammā in all its aspects». a- It is specific to the imperfect, so it jusses it and negates it and transfers it from the present time to the past, like the jussive «lam». b- It is specific to the past, requiring two clauses of which the second exists because of the existence of the first, as in «لما جاءني أكرمته» (when he came to me, I honoured him). Therefore it is called a particle of existence due to existence, and this is the temporal one. c- That it come as a particle of exception in the sense of «illā», and this enters the nominal clause, as in «إِنْ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ لَمَّا عَلَيْها حافِظٌ».
These are its three divisions, which we have presented to you in brief. This does not prevent us from pointing out that there are other partial matters, which whoever wishes can look for in the longer works.
14-

safi-cedvel:14-14.t:
* I'rab:
(يا) a particle of alert [Note: or a particle of vocative and lament; (ويلنا) is a vocative muḍāf of lament, accusative.], (ويلنا) an absolute object of an omitted verb, accusative.
Clause: «قالوا ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause: «يا ويلنا ... » has no grammatical position; parenthetical, for lament.
And the clause: «إنّا كنّا ظالمين ... » is in the position of an accusative, being the content of what was said.
And the clause: «كنّا ظالمين ... » is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of inna.
15-
